TERM OF REFERENCE

To ensure the implementation of the World Bank China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package I (Supervision Services)of the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulationand to achieve the informatization construction goals of the project, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to engage a third-party service agency to carry out the implementation of this project.

I. Background and Description

The World Bank Loan China Food Safety Demonstration Project officially entered into force on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period until March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety at both national and local levels. As a key implementer of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of 10 million US dollars and will precisely support the achievement of the project goals through the construction of six core sub-projects:

i. Develop a full-chain traceability platform for "coding, tracing, and recalling" food in key areas, enabling whole-process traceability and risk early warning with 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

ii. Build the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" system under the Guangdong Food Safety initiative, covering intelligent video supervision of scenarios such as elderly care and campus canteens;

iii. Upgrade and transform the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and improve the accident emergency response mechanism;

iv. Carry out a capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of skill competitions;

v. Establish a high-quality food standard system and conduct promotion activities, developing no less than 30 standards and carrying out quality monitoring within two years;

vi. Provide professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above-mentioned construction content, we plan to refer to advanced practices from other World Bank projects to further optimize procurement management and improve service coordination efficiency; in the next phase of actual procurement operations, while keeping the total project budget unchanged, we intend to integrate the supervision services of the four projects—the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Areas (or Key Varieties), the Guangdong Food Safety "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" System Construction Project, the Emergency Real-Time Dispatching and Command System Upgrade, Transformation, and Operation Project, and the Capacity Improvement Project for Food-Related Personnel in the Market Supervision Field—into a single package for unified procurement and management, so as to ensure the smooth achievement of the project's construction goals.

II. Objectives

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the informatization sub-projects under the World Bank Loan Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, third-party supervision services will be provided throughout the entire process for four informatization sub-projects: the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" full-chain traceability platform, the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" intelligent supervision system, the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and the learning and assessment system for capacity improvement of food-related personnel. Through full-cycle, closed-loop management and control covering quality, progress, investment, changes, contract compliance, safety, intellectual property, multi-party collaboration, and documentation during project construction, we will ensure that project construction activities are legal, compliant, economical, and scientific; strictly control risks such as project overspending, delays, and quality defects; and guarantee the project is completed with high quality within the agreed schedule and budget. With the core goal of comprehensively enhancing modern governance capacity for food safety, we will build a full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early warning response, and closed-loop disposal through the system construction and coordinated advancement of the informatization sub-projects. This will provide a solid data foundation and institutional guarantee for the scientific calculation of the "proportion of early warnings for which mitigation measures have been initiated," realize systematic training for food safety inspectors and supervisors while quantifying the participation ratio of female supervisors, comprehensively improve the quality and management level of project implementation, ensure that the collection, accounting, and reporting of all indicator data comply with World Bank standards, and help promote the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

III. Service Overview

The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 1.6003 million.

(I) Scope of Services

The service scope of this project covers the full-process supervision services for four informatization sub-projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Content

The supervision service agency shall provide full-process supervision services for the implementation of the aforementioned four informatization sub-projects, assisting the project undertaking company and the user party in carrying out their work to ensure the achievement of the predetermined project goals. In accordance with supervision work specifications, the agency shall implement full-process control over project quality, schedule, investment, contracts, and information security. This is to ensure that the construction activities are legal, compliant, reasonable, scientific, and economical, thereby reducing project construction risks and achieving both the overall project goals and the current phase goals.For details:

 

  1. Quality Control

Adopt a full-process control mechanism of pre-prevention, in-process management and control, and post rectification. Control the quality of system development in accordance with regulatory standards, project contracts and design documents; regularly review project documents, issue supervision briefs and conduct quantitative evaluation; assist in reviewing design schemes and software selection, and supervise software testing, installation and commissioning links; formulate project acceptance standards and disposal plans, urge the implementation unit to rectify quality defects and follow up the operation and maintenance services during the warranty period. Simultaneously control the training quality, review the training plan, supervise the implementation of training and recheck the training summary.
 

  1. Schedule Control
    Review the development schedule plans at all levels of the implementation unit and verify their feasibility; track the progress of requirements, coding, testing and online stages in real time, and urge dynamic adjustment of the construction period; put forward optimization schemes in a timely manner and urge implementation of rectification when there is a serious deviation in the construction period; realize visual control of development progress relying on standardized project management tools.
     
  2. Investment Control
    Optimize the software development implementation plan, reasonably control the costs of customized development, third-party component procurement, etc., to ensure the cost-effectiveness of capital investment; track the use of funds in real time, give early warning and adjustment suggestions in time if there is a large deviation in the budget, and strictly control the risk of overspending.
     
  3. Change Control
    Unify the management of various changes such as software requirements, functions, interfaces and architecture, and standardize the whole process of change application, impact assessment, multi-party review, approval and implementation, and regression testing; evaluate the impact of changes on quality, schedule, investment and safety, eliminate disorderly demand spread, completely retain the change ledger and complete the change filing of local government projects.
     
  4. contract management
    Assist the construction unit in drafting, reviewing and signing software development and supporting procurement contracts; track the performance of the contract throughout the process; coordinate the handling of construction period extension, change, breach of contract, claim, subcontracting and project dispute mediation; review the payment application of the implementation unit according to the contract terms and issue supervision review opinions.
     
  5. Document Information Management
    Unify the collection and management of a full set of software project materials such as requirements, design, testing, operation and maintenance, and training; regularly submit project dynamic materials to the construction unit; urge the implementation unit to sort out and file technical materials in accordance with specifications; transmit notices and contact sheets issued by the construction unit; report software quality problems to the superior immediately and supervise the closed-loop rectification.
     
  6. Safety and Intellectual Property Management
    Supervise the hierarchical protection of government business data and internal materials throughout the process to strictly prevent unauthorized access and leakage of data; control the operation safety of development, testing and online links, implement code security and relevant requirements of classified protection, and eliminate safety accidents. At the same time, protect the intellectual property rights of project development achievements, software source codes and customized functions, and strictly prohibit illegal reuse or private external transmission of achievements.
     
  7. Organization and Coordination

Establish a standardized project meeting mechanism, organize weekly meetings, demand coordination meetings, technical special meetings, problem notification meetings and phased acceptance meetings, and completely retain meeting minutes; coordinate the work relations among the construction unit, business departments, development and implementation units and software and hardware suppliers, and build a normalized communication channel; coordinate to solve various problems such as demand differences, development (stuck points), testing disputes, etc., and simultaneously implement the project safety supervision objectives.
(III) Service Period

The supervision service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029).

The Electricité du Cambodge (EDC) has obtained a grant from the World Bank’s Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) under the Cambodia Sustainable Energy Transition Project (CSET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  • The Project is designed to support the government’s priorities of strengthening the power grid and energy efficiency, while promoting cost-effective demand-side energy management to ensure energy stability, system resilience, and affordability.

 

  • To achieve these outcomes, the proposed Project aims to significantly: (i) strengthen power transmission and distribution infrastructure to increase capacity, enhance reliability; (ii) expand access to modern electricity services in remaining unelectrified rural areas; and (iii) implement energy efficiency and demand-side management measures across industrial and residential sectors. This integrated model reflects the direction outlined in Cambodia’s Revised PDP (2022–2040), NEEP (2022–2030), and broader socio-economic development agenda. By strengthening power infrastructure for VRE integration while improving energy productivity, the proposed Project will reduce system costs, increase new or improved access to energy, and strengthen industrial competitiveness. Doing both investment components together will position Cambodia for a more resilient, export-ready, and energy-secure economy.

 

  • The selected Consultant will support Project Management Unit of EDC to roll out preparation activities needed for EDC towards project approval by Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC). The Consultant will coordinate with EDC and other concerned government institutions to attain clearance and approval by government as necessary for negotiations, signing of legal agreement, and effectiveness of CSET. The assignment is expected to start in October 2026 with the contract duration of 3 months based on the need and Consultant’s performance and project extension.

 

  • QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Technical supervision for the Civil Works under “Construction of a museum near the Dvin archaeological site” & “Restoration, conservation, landscaping, and visitor infrastructure improvement works at the Dvin archaeological site”

TRIP-CQS-TS-01

1. PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP) aim to boost Armenia's tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and soft investments in several regions. It will support seven of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, culture, education, and ecotourism across Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Tavush, and Syunik regions. The project will improve connectivity to these clusters and enhance tourism site infrastructure. It also seeks to elevate Armenia’s natural assets and human resources, improving business and professional skills in nearby communities to maximize the job creation. Additionally, TRIP aligns with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment in these tourism clusters.

Infrastructure investment component of TRIP include construction of new public buildings including museum buildings, restoration and preservation of historical monuments, urban regeneration of old towns and villages, including restoration of building facades, public spaces, museums, roads and enhancement of cultural and natural heritage sites, including access and presentation.

Overall management and coordination of implementation and supervision of Project will be executed by the Armenian Territorial Development Fund (CLIENT).

The present terms of reference describe consulting services for supervision of civil works under TRIP sought by the CLIENT.

The consulting services ("the Services") include daily supervision of the civil works. The civil works contracts to be supervised will include a variety of works, such as construction of new and restoration of existing buildings and cultural heritage monuments/sights, touristic infrastructure, as well as municipal water/wastewater systems, lighting, local roads and utility services.

2. OBJECTIVES

The purpose of construction supervision is to execute technical supervision over the civil works to ensure high quality of the civil works, adherence to the terms of work execution provided for in the construction contracts in compliance with the detailed design and specification requirements, to ensure the reliability, long-term sustainability and efficient operation of the civil works.

The main objective of the assignment is the daily supervision of the  construction or/and rehabilitation works, as the Technical Supervision Consultant (Consultant) on behalf of the CLIENT in accordance with the provisions of the signed contracts between CLIENT and Contractors in order to ensure the following:

a) High quality of construction in adherence to the valid standards, regulations and laws of Armenia and international standards and best practices; 

b) Adherence to the requirements of valid design (draft, detailed), specifications and performance standards by implementation of the provisions of the technical specifications and other provisions of the works contracts;

c) Adherence to the national environmental, social and labor legislation and regulations, and the World Bank’s ESF, and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) applicable to TRIP,  as well as the site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) to be prepared for subprojects;

d) Completion of works in accordance with the works schedules and  contracts price.  

The tentative duration of this assignment is 30 months, plus defects liability period  after completion of each civil work  contract.

3. SCOPE OF SERVICES

  • Overall, the administration, execution and oversight of the “Civil Works to be implemented under the TRIP” will be organized via contract in three standard roles: Employer, Contractor, and Technical Supervision Consultant   
  • ATDF acts as the Client carrying out the overall and contractual coordination of the Project.
  • The Contractor executes the construction works.
  • The Consultant carries out daily technical supervision.

The Consultant shall review, assess, and provide recommendations on all engineering matters and technical decisions necessary for the efficient, timely, and successful implementation of the civil works contract, for the consideration and approval of the Employer.

The Consultant is directly responsible for daily supervision and immediate contacts with the works Contractors. Consultant will closely liaise with the Project Implementation and Supervision and Technical Supervision Departments of ATDF (CLIENT) to solve issues.

Consultant should ensure strict adherence of Contractors to the requirements of detailed designs, technical specifications, site-specific EMSPs, and Resettlement Plans (RPs).

The Consultant is responsible for mobilizing a team in compliance with the requirements and phases outlined below. The obligations include: providing all necessary personnel on site (engineers, supervisors, quality inspectors, environmental and social specialists, occupational health and safety (OHS) etc.) for the supervision of works, inspection and installation of the equipment, testing of construction materials, and monitoring the implementation of ESMPs and reporting.

Within ten (10) days after the signing of the Civil Works Contract the Consultant shall submit the detailed work plan of the technical supervision services (including scope of duties of each specialist of Consultant’s team) for Client’s approval. The Work Plan shall be aligned with the construction phases and tentative implementation schedule as well as a cost estimate indicating anticipated input (workday) of each specialist and covering all the costs related to supervision services.

Before the approval of the design documentation conduct a comprehensive, critical review of the proposed designs for each component by validating the necessary information obtained through Cadaster, local municipality, respective utility companies, etc. and via visiting the location of the contract site physically – and present written recommendations in the Inception Report regarding any necessary design changes or design aspects, which may pose implementation problems or unintended results during works.

 4. GENERAL AND SPECIFIC TASKS

4a. General Task

The tasks of the Consultant will include but not be limited to the following:

  1. Preparing a construction supervision work program to be prepared early during the Consultant’s contract commencement.
  2. Throughout the construction period, the Consultant shall undertake technical inspections and measurements to verify work quantities, maintain records of civil works, and certify completed works in accordance with reporting formats approved under the Contract.
  3. On a monthly basis, the Consultant shall prepare and submit to the Employer a report on quality-related issues, test results, non-compliances, identified defects, corrective actions and their resolution/implementation status.
  4. Reviewing the Contractors' payment certificates and giving respective feedback to CLIENT prior to approval by the latter;
  5. Verify the compliance between quantities and quality of executed works with the design and technical specifications; supervising adherence to the program and schedule of works to be executed by the Contractors;
  6. Supervising progress of preparation works (in accordance with the RA Construction Norms (RACN) 13-05-2026 "Organization of Construction Operations" and Order No. 09-A of the Chairman of the Urban Development Committee of the Republic of Armenia, dated 9 February 2023) to be executed by the Contractors, including construction of temporary structures in compliance with the work execution program and adherence to the terms provided for in the schedule; check and ensure that the Contractor has obtained all necessary permits and approvals from state and local governments, as well as utilities providers; and reporting, in writing, to the CLIENT.
  7. Check the safety of the works, property and personnel, and public in adherence to RACN regulations and TRIP site-specific E&S  instruments.
  8. Checking the compliance certifications of the construction materials used in construction (cement, aggregates, additives, reinforcement, metal constructions, precast concrete, bitumen, asphalt concrete elements, mineral materials, electrical cables, and water supply pipes,etc.), checking compliance of manufacturers’’ factory sample analysis and laboratory testing data with requirements of technical specifications and RACN;
  9. Reviewing and approving that installed equipment meets the specifications defined under the detailed design;
  10. Inspect compliance of as built drawings submitted by Contractors (endorsed by signature and sealed) with the executed works;
  11. Maintain a daily technical supervision register of works, implemented by the Contractor  making appropriate entries in the Construction Log maintained by the Contractor, recording observations, identified defects, and the measures taken for their rectification; receiving and concluding the phases of completed works with proper documents (certifications for hidden  works, tests and other documentation);
  12.  Conduct daily photography and video recording of construction activities performed, including these materials in the monthly reports and providing these materials upon Employer’s request. ;
  13. Certify completed stages of the Works in accordance with the format developed by the Consultant and approved by the Employer.
  14. Subject to the Employer’s approval, organize and supervise any additional unforeseen independent testing required to verify the final quality and compliance of the Works executed by the Contractor;
  15. In case of detecting defects or deficient works, compile a punch list setting deadlines for their rectification, immediately notify the Client in writing and monitor the rectification of these deficiencies.
  16. Observing and reviewing sampling, measurements and tests conducted by the Contractor (such as pressure tests for leaks) ensuring that the relevant records are prepared, for any works that are about to be covered or put out of view. In the event of identification of non-conformity with the RACNs, design requirements and/or specifications, prohibit the continuation of the works or the use of the materials, document such cases through appropriate formal records/acts and notifying the Employer in writing.
  17. Ensuring that Contractors have a good command of the requirements laid out in ESMPs, tracking adherence of Contractors’ performance with the ESMPs, and advising on and following the  implementation of the corrective actions in case of identified environmental and social non-compliances;
  18. Supervise Contractors’ compliance with labor management requirements, including enforcement of Codes of Conduct and the functioning of the workers’ grievance mechanism (GM) in line with Project Labor Management Procedures (LMP).
  19. Reviewing and making recommendations to the CLIENT Supervision Engineer for any requests for variation or change orders, and Contractors’ claims.
  20. Submitting periodic reports to the CLIENT in accordance with the requirements outlined in the Chapter on “Reporting” and Chapter on “Preparation of Reports and Submission Dates” of these TOR.
  21. Check and monitor the implementation of occupational safety briefings conducted by Contractors (in accordance with Inter-state Standard GOST 12.0.004-2015).

 

4b. Specific Tasks

The Consultant shall provide the following services under the direct guidance of the CLIENT:

  1. Inspect Contractors’ camps and temporary structures/buildings, storage areas, equipment and machinery to verify compliance with the applicable RACNs and detailed design requirements;
  2. Inspect quality and quantity of earthworks and foundation preparation: dimensions of foundation pits, trench’s cross sections, sand bedding, backfilling, quality of compacted fills, levels; gravel beds; lean concrete layers and etc;
  3. Supervise progress of concrete and reinforced concrete works. Inspect formwork dimensions, installation accuracy, quality, location of reinforcement and embedded parts, review of mix design, proper placement of concrete and testing resultant concrete strength, compliance of welded joints with the applicable RACNs;
  4. Supervise installation and repairs to the precast reinforced concrete constructions as well as inspection of dimensions, quality and placement of reinforced concrete elements, joint fillers, pads, water stops and other materials;
  5. Inspect reconstruction-restoration of buildings (architectural and structural parts); check conformance of supplied materials to the design requirements, specifications, and quality standards; inspect the workmanship of architectural and decorative elements of buildings; ensure application of the specified and approved technologies and materials; supervise strengthening of fundaments, supporting structures, seismic belts, change of roofs, building façade improvement containing brick finishing, plastering, changing of cornices, etc., rehabilitation of wooden, metallic and concrete balconies; rehabilitation of roofs (tile; soft roof, metal), rehabilitation of doors and windows, masonry works;
  6. Supervise and inspect road’ rehabilitation works: roadway pavement (different materials) layout of sidewalks, curbs, trails street furniture and etc.;
  7. Inspect installation of power cables, electrical equipment, lighting of streets, squares and parks;
  8. Inspect installation works of pressure and gravity pipelines (water supply, sewage, storm water) constructed of various materials (steel, cast iron, r/concrete, PE, PVC, etc.) including inspection of gradients, joints, fittings  and other accessories in accordance with construction codes and contract specifications and verify the conduct and availability of the observance and certification of pressure and other tests, including laboratory testing where applicable, to ensure that leakage, if any, does not exceed limits as provided under the technical specifications;
  9. Supervise progress of installation, mechanical and electrical equipment; after completion of interim phases of construction, test equipment together with Contractors and the CLIENT’s Supervision Engineer and certify that the tests met the requirements of the technical specifications;
  10. Inspect construction of water supply headworks, pumping stations, raw water treatment and wastewater treatment plants including start-up and commissioning of electrical and mechanical equipment; prior to the commissioning stage, review and approve the updated/detailed functional testing method and schedule submitted by the Contractor in line with the design specifications ; checking the results of functional tests;
  11. Check the installation of the pressure and gravity pipelines (waterlines, sewage, storm water) and laboratory/pressure test reports in accordance with the RACN;
  12. Inspect certificates of construction materials and equipment used during construction (electrical and mechanical equipment, pipes, valves, fire hydrants, flow meters, fittings, cement, inert materials, admixtures, reinforcement steel, metal-ware, pre-cast reinforced concrete elements, wooden and ceramic materials, road pavement materials and etc.); correspondence of data on sample analysis (carried out by the manufacturer in the factory) and laboratory tests to the requirements of the technical specifications and correspondence of construction materials used for restoration/conservation of physical cultural resources to the specifications and technological requirements of such works;  
  13. Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures in line with site-specific ESMPs in the course of works at each construction site; promptly notify the CLIENT on any deviations/violations of ESMP requirements, on any complaints from local communities related to ongoing works, and on any unforeseen issues affecting environment and/or cultural heritage which may emerge in the course of works; recommend remedial and/or corrective measures to the CLIENT and follow up on their application upon the CLIENT’s approval;  
  14. Oversee temporary on-site storage and final disposal of construction waste to the formally assigned sites or landfills and on the reinstatement of work sites upon completion of activity at any given one;
  15. Support effective implementation of Project Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanism (FGRM) at the local level in accordance with the Project Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and notify Project Coordinator on any issues appeared at the site.
  16. Inspect and oversee the implementation of by Operational Health and Security (OHS) measures, at the construction site, including the safety of structures used for work at heights and the proper use of appropriate PPE in accordance with site-specific ESMPs.
  17. Oversee implementation of community health and safety measures in accordance with site-specific ESMPs, including site safety, access control, traffic management, and ensure that community complaints related to health, safety, and nuisance are properly recorded, addressed, and reported through the FGRM.
  18. Verify that site-level information disclosure measures are in place, including appropriate signage and FGRM contact details, and verify that any access restrictions and safety requirements are clearly communicated to nearby residents in accordance with site-specific ESMPs.
  19. Promptly inform the Client about any accident and incident related to the project within 24 hours, that may have adversely affected the environment, communities, public or workers, for instance labor or transport related accidents that might result in serious injuries etc; participate in incident investigations and related reporting, as required by the Client, in line with the ESCP and applicable incident reporting procedures.

 

5. REPORTING

At the outset of the contract commencement, the Consultant shall elaborate a reporting system (systematic registration and submission of the appropriate documents) CLIENT to provide regular, complete and detailed information to the CLIENT on progress and quality of civil works.

The Consultant shall submit to the Client  the following reports:

  • Monthly Progress Report summarizing progress with the construction activities, problems encountered, updated planning, status of ESMP compliance and any outstanding issues deemed important by the Consultant. These reports shall have appended to them the daily technical supervision register of works (See item 13 of General Tasks) and filled out monthly environmental and social monitoring forms, as well as the physical and financial progress report for each CW site, along with the forecast for the next period.
  • Special reports as may be required if there are one or more problems that require immediate attention of the CLIENT.
  • Quarterly report on the period of work indicating progress on each subproject, course of activities, implementation of ESMPs, and any proposed changes to the work plan;
  • As built-drawings prepared by Contractors and confirmed by Consultant;
  • Final Project Completion report including Civil work contract data, contract variations, a table of actually completed works and disbursed funds by month, photographs, general comments on the Contractor's performance, an environmental and social final report, the results of the Acceptance Commission's work.

5a.Preparation of Reports and Submission Dates

          The above reports shall be presented in according to the following requirements:

  • All reports shall be prepared in Microsoft Word and Excel, and presented to the CLIENT as bound documents according to agreed quantities (see table hereafter), in both hard copies and electronic files.
  • Drawings will also be provided in hard copies and electronic forms (AutoCAD or compatible software). Reports should have attachments such as video and photo materials about the activity progress as evidence. 
  • The reports should be submitted in Armenian and English languages.

 

Reports (English and Armenian)

Date

  1. Monthly report

Within 7 days of next month

  1. Quarterly report

Within 7 days of  month next to each quarter

  1. Final Completion Report including confirmed as-built drawings

Within 7 days after receiving the signed hand-over/acceptance protocol

 

6. INPUT BY CLIENT

 

The CLIENT shall provide the Consultant with detailed design documentation, technical specifications, Project Environmental and Social Instruments, including the ESMPs, and other available documents needed for proper implementation of construction supervision for each subproject.

ATDF will appoint its own specialists/engineers for each subproject, who will work closely with the Consultant and perform contract management and final decision-making functions.

APPEL A CANDIDATURES

ASSISTANT(E) TECHNIQUE CHARGÉ(E) D’ACCOMPAGNER LE MINISTÈRE DE L’INDUSTRIALISATION ET DU DÉVELOPPEMENT DU SECTEUR PRIVÉ (MIDSP) DANS L’IDENTIFICATION, LA STRUCTURATION ET LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DE SES PROJETS PRIORITAIRES ET STRUCTURANTS

    Crédit IDA 78730

    AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV

    Date de lancement :  16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a obtenu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Transformation économique pour la croissance inclusive (PIC3). Une partie du crédit sera utilisée pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultance cité en objet.

2. La mission principale de l’Assistant technique chargé d’accompagner le Ministère de l’Industrialisation et du Développement du Secteur Privé (MIDSP) dans l’identification, la structuration et la mise en œuvre de ses projets prioritaires et structurants, est d’accompagner le MIDSP dans la préparation d’un cadre stratégique et de réforme intégré fondé sur cinq étapes clairement articulées : diagnostiquer les réalités institutionnelles et sectorielles, prioriser les filières et chaînes de valeur à fort potentiel, formuler les orientations stratégiques, réformes et projets structurants, élaborer le cadre stratégique intégré, puis définir les modalités opérationnelles de mise en œuvre, de coordination et de suivi-évaluation.

3. Les termes de référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site www.pic.mg

4. La Coordination Nationale du Projet PIC3 invite les candidats à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services cidessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Un consultant sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures de recrutement de Consultant Individuel de la Banque Mondiale définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les Fournitures, Travaux, Services autres que les Services de Consultants », 6ème édition – Février 2025. Les trois (03) candidats jugés pertinents, après évaluation des dossiers, seront invités pour un entretien.

5. L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

6. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications suivantes :

  • Diplôme universitaire de niveau Master au minimum en économie, planification, politiques publiques, développement industriel, gestion de projets, administration publique, entrepreneuriat, finance, droit des affaires ou tout autre domaine pertinent.
  • Expérience professionnelle d’au moins 7 à 10 ans dans l’élaboration de politiques publiques, de stratégies sectorielles, de réformes économiques, de plans d’actions ou de programmes de développement.
  • Expérience confirmée dans les domaines couverts par la mission, notamment le développement industriel, le secteur privé, les PME/PMI, l’entrepreneuriat, l’investissement, l’environnement des affaires ou le développement des chaînes de valeur.
  • Expérience de collaboration avec les administrations publiques et les parties prenantes économiques, notamment les ministères, structures publiques, partenaires techniques et financiers, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, secteur privé et acteurs régionaux.
  • Maîtrise des outils de planification stratégique, de gestion axée sur les résultats et de suivi-évaluation, ainsi que des méthodes de diagnostic, de formulation de plans d’actions et de conduite de consultations.
  • Excellentes capacités d’analyse, de rédaction, de synthèse et de facilitation, avec une aptitude démontrée à produire des documents stratégiques de qualité, animer des ateliers et travailler avec des équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Parfaite maîtrise du français écrit et oral.

7. Les candidats intéressés doivent envoyer exclusivement par mail leur dossier de candidature, sous format PDF, composé d’une lettre de motivation, d’un CV détaillé avec les références professionnelles, d’une copie certifiée du diplôme le plus élevé ainsi que les attestations de travail au plus tard le 30 septembre 2026 à minuit à l’adresse : procurement@pic.mg

8. L’objet du mail d’envoi doit porter obligatoirement la mention suivante : AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV « AT ACCOMPAGNEMENT MIDSP »

Le Projet décline la responsabilité de la nonconsidération des candidatures ne respectant pas cette disposition obligatoire.

 

Antananarivo le 16 septembre 2026

Le Coordonnateur National du Projet PIC3

RAKOTONDRAZAKA Ladislas Adrien

Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Department of Youth Development

Economic Acceleration and Resilience for NEET (EARN) Project

Level-19, National Sports Council Tower

Purana Paltan, Dhaka-1000

www.dyd.gov.bd

 

Memo No.:  34.01.0000.046.38.137.26-                                        Date: 6 September 2026

 

Request For Expression of Interest

(Consulting Services – Firm Selection)

 

Country                      : Bangladesh

Project Name              : Economic Acceleration and Resilience for NEET (EARN)

Credit No.                   : IDA-7364-BD

Assignment Title         : Selection of Training Service Provider for skill enhancement of the officials and instructors of DYD under IDP Procurement.

Reference No.              : Package No. S43

  1. The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Economic Acceleration and Resilience for NEET (EARN) Project (P178077) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) will include but not limited to the following key tasks: The TMF will provide comprehensive technical, operational, and implementation support to design, develop, and roll out a structured capacity development program for DYD instructors and Upazila-level Youth Development Officers (YDOs), DDs and ADs, in district level and DYD Headquarters (HQ) officials in line with findings and key recommendations of the TNA and the EARN Project Implementation Roadmap.

Eligibility Criteria (Mandatory Criteria)

  1. The Department of Youth Development (DYD) invites eligible Consultants (firm) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants (Single Entity/All Partners of JV) should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Eligible Consultants (Firm) means any consultant (firm) shall have (i) Certificate of Incorporation/Evidence demonstrating that the consultant is a legally constituted/registered entity under the appropriate laws of the country of establishment; (ii) Valid trade license (valid up to June 2026), (iii) Tax Registration Certificate along with updated Tax Return Certificate (Up to Tax Year 2024-2025) and (iv) VAT Registration Certificate with BIN.
  2. In case of foreign consultant all documents must be submitted in translated English Version (certified copy) along with original copy indicating clearly (i) Certification of Incorporation/ Evidence demonstrating that the consultant is a legally constituted/registered entity under the appropriate laws of the country of establishment;  (ii) Trade License (Updated up to June 2026), (iii) Tax Registration Certificate and Tax Return Certificate (Up to Tax Year 2024-2025), (iv) VAT Registration Certificate with BIN as under appropriate laws of the country of establishment.
  3. Joint Venture and Authorization/Power of Attorney:
  1. Joint Venture (JV) shall be formed with maximum of four (4) partners including the lead partner. In case of JV agreement, the agreement shall be as per government rules of EOI submitting lead partners’ country/in case of intent to form JV, the letter of intent to form JV shall be in the “Letter Head Pad” of each partner.
  2. Letter of Authorization: The authorization letter/power of attorney shall include Name, Address, Designation and NID number and original signature of both the authority and authorized representative.
  1. If any single entity and/or the lead partner of the JV and/or any partner of the JV submits more than one Expression of Interest (EoI), either individually or as a JV partner, all EoIs submitted will be rejected. However, this does not preclude a firm’s (single entity and/or the lead partner of the JV and/or any partner of the JV) participation as a sub-consultant, or an individual’s (Key Experts) participation as a team member, in that package.

Shortlisting Criteria

  1. The shortlisting of the Consultants will depend upon a set of criteria, encompassing factors such as the agency's relevance to the scope of work relevant experience, specializations in the arena of the above-mentioned expertise. Any interested consultant (firm) must meet the following criteria to be shortlisted:
    1. General Experience (for all cases the years will be counted backward from the date of publishing of REOI):
      1. Single Entity: Experience in conducting nationwide training program and/or training of government officials of at least 7 (seven) years.
      2. Joint Venture - Lead Partner: Experience in conducting nationwide training program and/or training of government officials for minimum 7 (seven) years.
      3.  Joint Venture - Each Non-Lead Partner: Experience in conducting nationwide training program and/or training of government officials for minimum 5 (five) years.
    2. Specific Experience: (A Completion Certificate specifying (i) the actual contract/assignment amount and (ii) the period of the assignment is required as evidence to establish the consultant’s specific experience):
      1. Single Entity: Experience in conducting nationwide training program and/or training of government officials of at least two (2) contracts of total value at least BDT. 8.00 (eight) crore or equivalent USD (USD Exchange rate of Bangladesh Bank as on the last date of submission of REOI) during last 5 (five) years.
      2. The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to support the preparation and implementation of an Aged Asset Replacement Program covering selected hydropower generation and power network assets.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise the development of an Aged Asset Replacement Policy and Plan, identification and prioritisation of replacement projects, environmental and social screening and assessment, preparation of an implementation and procurement framework, and development of procurement documentation for the first batch of priority investments.

The Services will cover:

•    Review of EFL’s existing aged asset replacement policies and procedures, including risk evaluation and recommended improvements.

•    Stakeholder consultations and preparation of a stakeholder engagement plan aligned with applicable environmental and social requirements.

•    Development of a new Aged Asset Replacement Policy consistent with Good International Industry Practice and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework.

•    Assessment of the Wainiqeu and Nagado hydropower stations and the identified network substations, switchboards, transformers and related assets.

•    Project identification, prioritisation, cost estimates, economic analysis, environmental and social screening, risk classification and preparation of proportionate management instruments.

•    Development of a procurement strategy, technical specifications, bills of quantity and draft bidding documents, including relevant environmental and social provisions.

•    Knowledge transfer and training for relevant EFL personnel, together with a final implementation roadmap and recommendations.

  1. Background and Context

Fiji's energy sector plays a central role in the economic development, investment in climate resilience renewable energy projects, and ensure long-term sustainability of the Fijian Economy. The country's electricity supply is dominated by Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), a majority owned government utility responsible for the generation, transmission, distribution, and retail of electricity. EFL currently produces approximately 93 percent of electricity, with Independent Power Producers (IPPs) contributing the remaining balance.

EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

 

Some of EFL’s major power generation assets (Renewable/thermal) have gone past their useful or replacement life due to their old age. The age of these generation assets is over 20 years or more. Some generators have long been out of production with spare parts no longer available or have become obsolete.

EFL has over the years worked on a number of projects to replace its ageing assets in both the Generation and Network Areas. Some were funded through debt funding and the remaining through EFL’s internal cashflow with progress subject to availability of funds.

The Government of Fiji (GoF), supported by the World Bank under the proposed Fiji Energy Transformation Project, is committed to assisting Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) in the implementation of EFL’s Aged Asset Replacement program, and the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) is used to support this ageing assets screening and preparation.

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The primary objectives of this consultancy are to:

  1. Develop an Aged Asset Replacement policy for EFL, aligned with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESS);
  2. Establish an Aged Asset Replacement Plan; and
  3. Develop a framework for the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan in an efficient, cost-effective and transparent manner, aligned with the World Bank’s ESS.

The Aged Asset Replacement Policy should address the following:

  1. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  2. Establish clear, transparent, and competitive procurement processes for the implementation of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan;
  3. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers.
  4. Promote Good International Industry Practices (GIIP) in terms of environmental sustainability and social safeguards.

Specifically, the Consultancy should address the following:

  1. Identify ageing assets to be replaced or rehabilitated. A list is provided, with detailed information below.
  2. Promote energy-efficient replacement technologies
  3. Conduct a comprehensive E & S risk screening and assessment, including the corresponding mitigation measures / management plans, for all identified generation and substation upgrade, covering hazardous material handling, recovery (likelihood ACM in the switchboards, PCB and SF6 in the transformers etc.), waste disposal, emissions, and community impacts.
  4. Investment needs, and cost benefits analysis
  5. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  6. Proposed implementation plan, including procurement packaging
  7. Draft bidding documents, BoQ and Technical Specifications, or other procurement documents.
  8. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers including community safety awareness, emergency preparedness, and communication strategies to inform residents of planned outages or risks.

 

  1. Scope of Work

The aged assets include both aged hydropower stations and power network.

Two hydropower power stations are proposed to be assessed:

  1. Wainiqeu Hydro Power Station: Upgrade of Power Station and Equipment. Rehabilitate Penstock pipeline, weir and headpond
  2. Nagado Hydro Power Station: Upgrade of Power Station and Equipment. Rehabilitate Penstock pipeline, weir and headpond

The Consultant will carry out the following tasks for above two hydropower stations and power network:

Task 1: Review of the Existing Aged Asset Replacement Policies/Procedures

  • Risk evaluation of asset replacement projects, including impacts on air, water, waste, and community health, and propose measures for policy improvement.

Task 2: Stakeholder Consultations

  • Prepare a stakeholder engagement plan in accordance with ESS requirements.
  • Review current policy/procedures for EFL Aged Asset Replacement with Generation Department and EFL’s Environment & Social Safeguard specialists to ensure community safety assessments, emergency preparedness plans, and communication strategies are incorporated in the policy together with effective grievance redress mechanisms for affected stakeholders.
  • Meet with relevant Network Managers and Engineers to review current policy/procedures for Aged Asset Replacement.

Task 3: Development of a new Aged Asset Replacement Policy

Task 4: Project Identification

  • To establish which projects can be undertaken as part of the Fiji Energy Transformation Project.
  • Work with EFL to prioritize the projects approved to be undertaken under the Fiji Energy Transformation Project.
  • E&S screening and risk classification for the selected projects. See annex for more details.
  • Cost estimates and economic analysis

Task 5: Environmental and Social Assessment and Management

All assessments and instruments shall comply with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable national environmental legislation of Fiji (including the Environment Management Act 2005 and associated regulations), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP). More details are provided in the annex.

Task 6: Develop Procurement Strategy and Bidding Documents

  • Liaise with both EFL and MoF to develop procurement strategy to replace the identified aged assets.
  • Draft the bidding documents for the first batch of ageing assets to be replaced, mainly bills of quantity and technical specifications, including relevant E&S provisions.
  • Conduct training of relevant EFL personnel on the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Task 7: Final Report and Recommendations

  • Prepare a comprehensive final report consolidating all findings, the stakeholder consultation process, the proposed Aged Asset Replacement Policy and an Aged Asset Replacement implementation roadmap.
  • Present findings and recommendations to the relevant stakeholders.

  1. Ethical Standards and Conflict of Interest

The Consultant must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest at the time of proposal submission and throughout the duration of the assignment. Any firm or individual with a direct commercial interest in the Fiji electricity sector may be subject to additional scrutiny or disqualification.

 

 

Annex. E&S Screening, Risk Classification, and E&S Assessment and Management

 

E&S Screening and Risk Classification

As part of the project identification and prioritization process, the Consultant shall conduct an Environmental and Social (E&S) screening of all assets and sub-projects identified for potential inclusion under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. The purpose of this screening is to identify, at an early stage, the nature and significance of potential environmental and social risks and impacts associated with each sub-project, and to classify them accordingly to inform prioritization and downstream assessment requirements under Task 5.

The E&S screening shall be carried out in accordance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and shall include the following activities:

(a) Screening Checklist Development. The Consultant shall develop a standardized E&S screening checklist, to be reviewed and approved by EFL and the World Bank, covering the following parameters for each sub-project or asset replacement activity:

  • Nature, scale, and location of the proposed asset replacement works (e.g., generation assets, transmission and distribution infrastructure, substations, switchboards, transformers, and hydropower plant components);
  • Proximity to environmentally sensitive areas, including watercourses, riparian zones, protected areas, forests, and ecologically significant habitats;
  • Proximity to communities, settlements, sacred sites, and areas of cultural heritage significance;
  • Land access requirements, including temporary or permanent land acquisition, easements, or restrictions on land use;
  • Potential for generation of hazardous waste, including oils, asbestos-containing materials (ACM), SF6 gas, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), and other legacy contaminants associated with aging electrical infrastructure;
  • Potential for impacts on labor and working conditions, occupational health and safety, and community health and safety during works; and
  • Potential for disproportionate impacts on vulnerable or marginalized groups, including women, youth, and indigenous communities.

(b) Application of the Screening Checklist. The Consultant shall apply the approved screening checklist to each sub-project or asset cluster identified in Task 4, drawing on available data, site reconnaissance findings, and stakeholder inputs gathered under Task 2. For hydropower-related asset replacements, the screening shall additionally assess:

  • The potential for works to alter water release regimes, turbine operations, or intake structures in ways that may affect downstream river flows, including environmental flows (eflows);
  • Potential impacts on aquatic ecosystems, freshwater biodiversity, and ecosystem services dependent on river flows; and
  • Any associated civil works within or adjacent to river corridors, including intake structures, penstocks, tailraces, and powerhouses.

(c) E&S Risk Classification. Based on the screening outcomes, the Consultant shall assign each sub-project or asset replacement activity a preliminary E&S risk classification consistent with the World Bank ESF risk categories (High, Substantial, Moderate, or Low). The classification shall consider both the type and scale of potential impacts and the sensitivity of the receiving environment and social context.

(d) Screening Report. The Consultant shall prepare an E&S Screening Report summarizing the results of the screening exercise for all sub-projects. The report shall include, for each sub-project: the completed screening checklist, the preliminary E&S risk classification, the rationale for the classification, and recommended E&S assessment and management measures required under Task 5. The Screening Report shall form an input to the Project Identification deliverable and shall be shared with EFL, the Ministry of Finance, and the World Bank for review and clearance prior to finalization.

The outcomes of the E&S screening shall directly inform the selection and sequencing of sub-projects for the first batch of implementation, ensuring that sub-projects with manageable E&S risks are prioritized, and that appropriate assessment and management measures are in place before procurement commences.

 

 

Environmental and Social Assessment and Management

Building on the E&S screening conducted under Task 4, the Consultant shall undertake Environmental and Social (E&S) assessments and prepare the corresponding management instruments for the sub-projects identified for the implementation under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. All assessments and instruments shall comply with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable national environmental legislation of Fiji (including the Environment Management Act 2005 and associated regulations), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP).

    1. Scope and Approach

The E&S assessment shall cover all sub-projects in the first batch, as identified and screened under Task 4, including but not limited to:

  • Replacement of aged switchboards, transformers, and associated substation equipment across EFL's network;
  • Rehabilitation or replacement of generation assets at EFL's hydropower stations as identified under in the main text; and
  • Any associated civil, structural, or access works.

The scale and depth of assessment shall be proportionate to the E&S risk classification assigned to each sub-project under Task 4.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Assessment — Hydropower Asset Replacement

For asset replacement activities at hydropower stations, the Consultant shall prepare a standalone E&S assessment addressing the specific environmental and social sensitivities associated with hydropower infrastructure. The ESIA shall be prepared by qualified environmental and social specialists and shall include, at minimum, the following components:

 

(a) Description of the Existing Environment and Baseline Conditions

The Consultant shall compile and, where necessary, supplement existing baseline data to characterize the environmental and social baseline for each hydropower site and its area of influence, including:

  • Hydrology and water resources: river flow regimes, seasonal variability, historical discharge data, and existing water abstractions or diversions;
  • Aquatic ecology: species composition, abundance, and distribution of freshwater fish, macroinvertebrates, and other aquatic biota in rivers upstream and downstream of each facility;
  • Riparian and terrestrial ecology: vegetation communities, wildlife habitats, and any protected or endemic species in the project area;
  • Water quality: existing water quality conditions in receiving waterbodies;
  • Ecosystem services: identification and characterization of ecosystem services provided by river systems and dependent on flow regimes, including provisioning services (fisheries, water supply for downstream communities and agriculture), regulating services (flood attenuation, water purification), and cultural services (recreational, spiritual, and cultural values associated with rivers); and
  • Social baseline: communities and livelihoods dependent on river resources downstream of each facility, including subsistence fishing, smallholder irrigation, and cultural or ceremonial uses of water.

 

(b) Environmental Flow (E-Flow) Assessment

Given the small scale of the hydropower facility, the Consultant shall conduct a proportionate desktop E-flow review rather than a full E-flow assessment study. The review shall be commensurate with the nature of the asset replacement works and the associated level of hydrological risk.

The desktop review shall:

  • Document the existing operational flow regime at the facility, including any minimum flow release requirements specified in the facility's existing operating licence, consent conditions, or EFL operational procedures;
  • Confirm whether the proposed asset replacement works involve any physical changes to the intake structure, diversion weir, penstock, or tailrace that could alter the volume, timing, or continuity of water diverted or released — and if no such changes are proposed, note this explicitly as a basis for scoping out a detailed E-flow assessment;
  • Apply a simple hydrological desktop method — such as the Tennant (Montana) Method using available mean annual flow data — to provide a reference check on whether existing minimum flow releases at the facility are broadly consistent with accepted thresholds for maintaining basic ecological functions in the downstream river reach; and
  • Based on the above, conclude either that: (i) existing minimum flow provisions are adequate and no additional E-flow measures are required; or (ii) a gap exists that warrants a specific operational protocol or condition to be incorporated into the ESMP.

 

(c) Impact Assessment

The Consultant shall identify, predict, and evaluate the significance of potential environmental and social impacts associated with hydropower asset replacement works, covering both the construction and operational phases. Key impact pathways to be assessed shall include:

  • Changes to downstream flow regimes during works (e.g., dewatering, cofferdam installation, temporary flow diversion) and their effects on aquatic habitats, species, and ecosystem services;
  • Alteration of sediment transport and geomorphic processes resulting from changes to turbine operation or intake structures;
  • Impacts on aquatic biodiversity, particularly fish passage and migration, arising from works at intake or tailrace structures;
  • Risks of water quality degradation from construction activities, including turbidity, sedimentation, and potential release of oils, lubricants, or hazardous materials;
  • Hazardous waste generation and management, including oils, asbestos-containing materials, PCBs, SF6 gas, and other materials associated with aged electrical and mechanical equipment;
  • Community health and safety risks
  • Impacts on downstream communities dependent on river-based livelihoods and ecosystem services.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs)

The Consultant shall prepare ESMPs for each sub-project in the first batch, integrating findings from the E&S assessment (for hydropower facilities) and the E&S screening assessments. The ESMPs shall:

  • Describe, for each identified impact, the proposed hierarchy of mitigation measures (avoidance, minimization, mitigation, and compensation or offset where residual impacts remain);
  • Include specific management measures for: hazardous waste handling and disposal (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6); erosion and sediment control during civil works; hydropower operational protocols to maintain E-flows during construction phases; worker health and safety; community health and safety;
  • Specify monitoring requirements, including parameters to be monitored, monitoring locations, frequency, responsible parties, and reporting arrangements, with particular attention to downstream aquatic ecology and water quality monitoring at hydropower sites;
  • Define institutional responsibilities for ESMP implementation, supervision, and reporting within EFL;
  • Include a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) consistent with World Bank ESF requirements, covering all project-affected communities; and
  • Include an estimated budget for ESMP implementation.

 

    1. Stakeholder Engagement and Disclosure

In coordination with Task 2, the Consultant shall support EFL in conducting targeted stakeholder consultations on the E&S assessment and ESMP findings for each sub-project. Consultations shall be conducted in accordance with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan developed under Task 2, and shall be culturally appropriate and accessible to women, indigenous communities, and other vulnerable groups. Consultation records, including attendance, issues raised, and responses, shall be documented and appended to the ESIA and ESMP.

 

    1. Integration of E&S Requirements into Bidding Documents

The Consultant shall work closely with the procurement specialist engaged for Task 6 to ensure that all relevant E&S requirements are systematically integrated into the bidding documents for the asset replacement sub-projects. This shall include:

(a) E&S Specifications and Requirements. The Consultant shall prepare an Environmental and Social Requirements (ESR) section to be included within the bidding documents for each contract package, covering: Contractor obligations with respect to ESMP implementation, including preparation and submission of a Contractor Environmental and Social Management Plan (C-ESMP) prior to commencement of works; specific technical requirements for hazardous waste management (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6, and other hazardous materials from aged equipment), including approved disposal or recycling methods, handling procedures, and documentation requirements;

(b) E&S Performance Standards in Contract Conditions. The Consultant shall recommend appropriate contract conditions and performance standards to ensure contractor compliance with E&S requirements, including provisions for: submission and approval of the C-ESMP as a condition precedent to commencement of works; regular E&S reporting by the contractor;  and consequences for non-compliance, including stop-work orders and financial remedies.

(c) E&S Rated Criteria. The Consultant shall recommend criteria for evaluating contractor E&S capacity and performance as part of the qualification and evaluation criteria for each bidding package, covering contractor experience with E&S management on similar infrastructure projects, availability of qualified E&S personnel, and approach to hazardous materials management.
