REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499) - Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

International Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567224-CS-INDV

Reference No.

EOI-04/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise specialist environmental and social support to EFL's Project Preparation Unit. The Consultant will lead preparation of appraisal-stage environmental and social instruments, integrate requirements of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework into technical and procurement outputs, support policy and regulatory reviews, and prepare a procurement-ready terms of reference for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional Environmental and Social Management System.

 

The Services will cover:

• general environmental and social support to the Project Preparation Unit, including screening, risk-register management, ESCP inputs, coordination and practical capacity building;

• preparation of E&S scoping studies with critical-habitat screening, a site-specific ESMP for aging asset replacement, an RPF, negotiated land agreement due diligence, an integrated SEP, and LMP;

• preparation of a procurement-ready TOR for development and operationalization of EFL's institutional ESMS;

• environmental and social review of Electricity Act amendments, Rooftop Solar PV Policy, and private-sector renewable-energy participation;

• E&S inputs to the National control-centre upgrade, , aging power-infrastructure, grid-interconnection, hydropower and solar PV/BESS studies and concept designs; and

• monthly and quarterly reporting, disclosure support and an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary.

 

Implementation period: The assignment is expected to be part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and availability of GFPP financing.

 

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

 

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers concerning conflict of interest.

 

EOI Evaluation Criteria

Criterion

Weight

1. Relevant E&S assessment and management experience for infrastructure or energy projects

25%

2. Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMP, land/resettlement, SEP/GRM and LMP instruments

30%

3. Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC

20%

4. Relevant renewable-energy, grid infrastructure, hazardous-materials, Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance

15%

5. Qualifications, writing, coordination, consultation and capacity-building capability

10%

Total

100%

 

Form and content of the Expression of Interest:

Expressions of interest should contain only the information necessary to assess the criteria above. Consultants should submit a curriculum vitae and a concise statement demonstrating relevant assignments and experience.

A financial proposal is not required at this stage.

The Consultant assessed as best qualified against the criteria will be invited to negotiate a contract in accordance with the applicable procurement arrangements.

Submission

Further information may be obtained by emailing tenders@efl.com.fj during office hours, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Fiji Time, Monday to Friday, no later than three clear days before the closing date.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded to the EFL e-Tender Portal (TenderLink) at https://www.tenderlink.com/efl by registering your company, by 4:00 PM (1600 hrs) Fiji Time on Wednesday, 30th September 2026.

EOI documents may be viewed and downloaded from www.efl.com.fj(opens in new window) or https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window).

Submissions by email or facsimile will not be accepted. Hard-copy submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

 

 

Appendix 1 - Terms of Reference

TERMS OF REFERENCE

INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL (E&S) SPECIALIST

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) - Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)

1. Introduction and Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499), a World Bank-supported initiative estimated at USD 230 million. The project aims to accelerate renewable-energy development, modernize the power grid, rehabilitate aging infrastructure, and reform the power sector to attract private investment in solar energy. Key interventions span Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni, including solar PV/BESS parks of more than 50 MW each, grid-evacuation infrastructure, transmission-line upgrades and modernization of existing power stations.

The Initial Environmental and Social Review Summary has classified the project's environmental and social risks as Substantial, reflecting biodiversity impacts, customary iTaukei land tenure, community health and safety, labor influx, SEA/SH risks, and supply-chain concerns associated with PV modules and battery energy storage systems.

EFL is establishing a Project Preparation Unit (PPU) to prepare the project for appraisal and Board approval. The E&S Specialist will lead preparation of required E&S instruments, integrate E&S requirements into technical and procurement outputs, and prepare the TOR for a separate capacity-building assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The objective is to ensure that GFPP-financed preparation activities and the investments they support comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, applicable Fiji law, and Good International Industry Practice.

3. Scope of Work

The Consultant will perform the following tasks, organized into five functional areas:

3.1 General E&S Support to the PPU

• Serve as the PPU's E&S focal point and advise the Project Manager and technical teams on application of the ESF.

• Screen preparation activities and concept designs, identify applicable standards and instruments, and maintain an E&S Risk Register with actions, responsibilities and status.

• Prepare ESCP inputs, TORs for specialized studies, and E&S requirements for technical specifications and bidding documents; oversee related consultant outputs.

• Provide practical ESF training and on-the-job support to the PPU and relevant EFL staff.

• Coordinate with the World Bank, relevant Fiji agencies, TLTB, technical consultants and EFL departments, and maintain records of key decisions and actions.

3.2 Preparation of E&S Instruments Required by Appraisal

This is the most critical function of the assignment. The E&S Specialist will prepare the following appraisal-stage instruments and related outputs:

a. E&S Scoping Studies with Critical Habitat Screening

• Lead scoping studies for solar PV/BESS parks on Vanua Levu and Taveuni, grid-evacuation infrastructure, and new or upgraded transmission lines.

• Conduct structured Critical Habitat screening under ESS6 using available biodiversity data, including IUCN Red List species, Fiji endemic avifauna information, and protected-area registries.

• Where critical habitat is identified or cannot be ruled out, prepare detailed assessments and, where necessary, a Biodiversity Management Plan with offset strategies, no-go zones and seasonal restrictions.

• Include baseline social surveys, land-tenure mapping, community presence, vulnerable-group identification, and climate-resilience considerations such as cyclone, flooding and sea-level-rise risks.

b. Environmental and Social Management Plan - Aging Asset Replacement

• Prepare a site-specific ESMP for rehabilitation and replacement of aging power infrastructure under Component 3, covering baseline conditions, construction and operational risks, hazardous materials including PCBs, asbestos and e-waste, mitigation, monitoring, emergency response, contractor requirements, responsibilities, schedules and costs.

c. Resettlement Policy Framework

• Prepare an RPF consistent with ESS5 covering legal and institutional arrangements and gap analysis; eligibility and cut-off dates; entitlements and replacement-cost valuation; livelihood restoration; procedures for site-specific plans; consultation and grievance arrangements; monitoring, responsibilities and budget provisions.

d. Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report

• Identify and document all project sites or corridors where land or access rights have been or may be secured through negotiated settlement or other voluntary arrangement, and verify consistency with ESS5 and Fiji law.

• Prepare an inventory of leases, easements, access and land-use agreements, donations, transfers and other consensual arrangements, recording parcels, rights-holders, status, duration, consideration, benefits and supporting evidence.

• Assess whether each arrangement is voluntary, transparent, informed and free from coercion; whether formal, informal, customary, secondary and shared rights-holders were identified and represented; and whether participants had sufficient information, time, advice and a genuine right to refuse.

• For customary land and resources, screen whether ESS7 and FPIC apply. Where required, document a culturally appropriate collective process through institutions selected by affected iTaukei communities, with participation of women, youth and potentially excluded rights-holders. Do not infer FPIC solely from approvals by TLTB, agencies or individual owners.

• Where applicable, confirm and document eligibility cut-off dates, culturally appropriate public notice, valuation and compensation or benefit methodology, replacement-cost consistency, implementation status, grievances and corrective actions.

• Conclude for each arrangement whether ESS5 criteria are demonstrated and identify any additional instrument, remedial action, responsible party and completion deadline required before access or civil works.

e. Integrated Stakeholder Engagement Plan

• Prepare a project-level SEP consistent with ESS10, including stakeholder analysis, differentiated engagement for disadvantaged or vulnerable groups, disclosure, responsibilities, schedule, monitoring and reporting.

• Include a culturally appropriate consultation plan for communities potentially affected by solar PV/BESS and associated infrastructure, covering languages, timing, representation, feedback, land arrangements, benefit sharing and any ESS7 FPIC process.

• Establish an accessible project grievance mechanism and a confidential, survivor-centered SEA/SH reporting and referral pathway.

f. Labor Management Procedures

• Prepare LMP consistent with ESS2 for direct, contracted, community and primary supply workers, including applicable law and gaps, terms and conditions, OHS, emergency preparedness, accommodation, labor influx, child and forced labor, PV/BESS supply-chain due diligence, codes of conduct, worker grievances, contractor obligations and training.

g. TOR for Development and Operationalization of EFL's ESMS

• Prepare a procurement-ready TOR and supporting inputs for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS including potential staffing and structure to ensure the ESMS is properly resourced, strategically aligned, and embedded within EFL for lasting effectiveness.

• Define objectives, scope, methodology, deliverables, schedule, expertise, coordination, knowledge transfer and acceptance criteria. Cover policy and governance; screening; stakeholder, labor, land, biodiversity, pollution, community-safety, cultural-heritage, contractor and supply-chain management; incident response; monitoring; reporting; tools; templates; training; and a time-bound implementation plan.

• Consult relevant EFL departments. This assignment does not include development or implementation of the ESMS.

3.3 Policy and Regulatory Support

• Review proposed amendments to Fiji's Electricity Act from an E&S perspective, identify gaps with the World Bank ESF and international good practice, and recommend measures for the revised policy.

• Review the proposed Rooftop Solar PV Policy from an E&S perspective, including potential effects on consumers, community uptake and grid workers.

• Advise on E&S requirements for private-sector renewable-energy participation, including application of IFC Performance Standards and World Bank ESF requirements to PPP or private-investment components.

• Assess EFL's potential for an Environmental and Social Policy and support EFL's E&S team to derive and implement a practical policy.

3.4 E&S Inputs to Technical Studies and Infrastructure Components

• National Control Center Upgrade: identify E&S risks associated with civil works, OHS, asbestos and PCBs, and recommend mitigation for technical specifications.

• Modernization of Nabouwalu Government Station: conduct site-specific screening, identify community-proximity, worker-community and hazardous-material risks, and prepare an ESMP if required.

• Aging Infrastructure Rehabilitation: supplement the Component 3 ESMP with screening and, where feasible, inspection of all proposed sub-sites for hazardous materials, cultural heritage and social risks.

• Power Grid Interconnection, Vanua Levu-Taveuni: support feasibility and engineering studies with environmental and social routing-alternatives analysis and identification of a preferred route based on E&S criteria.

• Hydropower: prepare assessment TOR requirements covering direct, indirect, induced and cumulative life-cycle impacts across the relevant catchment, including flows, sediment, biodiversity, ecosystem services, water use, livelihoods, land, safety, cultural heritage, associated facilities, alternatives, mitigation, monitoring and adaptive management.

• Solar PV/BESS Parks: provide E&S inputs to concept designs for two parks of more than 50 MW each, including environmentally and socially informed site-selection criteria and ESF compliance review.

3.5 Monitoring, Reporting and Disclosure

• Submit monthly E&S progress reports covering instrument preparation, risk-register actions, engagement, grievances, emerging issues and preparation-phase ESCP commitments.

• Prepare quarterly stakeholder-engagement summaries.

• Coordinate disclosure through EFL and other required channels and make accessible copies available to affected communities.

• Prepare an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary recording instrument status, review, disclosure, outstanding actions and post-appraisal timelines.

4. Methodology

• Desktop review of project, legal, technical and E&S documentation and available baseline data.

• Structured screening, site visits and physical inspections where feasible.

• Stakeholder consultations with EFL, government agencies, TLTB, affected communities, technical consultants and the World Bank.

• Application of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, applicable Fiji law, GIIP and the mitigation hierarchy.

• Iterative preparation, review and revision of instruments, with clear evidence trails, action tracking and quality assurance.

• Practical knowledge transfer and on-the-job support to EFL and PPU personnel.

5. Key Deliverables

All deliverables shall be submitted in English, professionally edited, and formatted in accordance with any World Bank templates provided.

6. Reporting and Coordination

The E&S Specialist will report to the PPU Project Manager on a day-to-day basis. For technical E&S matters, the Specialist will coordinate closely with World Bank E&S Specialists and participate in World Bank supervision missions and project-preparation meetings.

The Specialist will also coordinate with:

• EFL's full-time Environmental Officer and Social Officer, once recruited;

• GFPP technical consultants in engineering, energy and finance;

• iTaukei Land Trust Board on land-tenure and customary-engagement matters;

• Department of Environment and other relevant Fiji government agencies; and

• external E&S consultants engaged for specialized studies.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

• University degree, at minimum Bachelor's level, in environmental science, social science, natural-resource management, engineering or a closely related field. A postgraduate qualification in environmental or social assessment is strongly preferred.

7.2 Professional Experience

• At least seven years of relevant experience in E&S assessment and management for infrastructure or energy projects.

• Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMPs, land or resettlement instruments, SEPs/GRMs and LMPs.

• Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land and resettlement due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC.

• Experience with hazardous materials, renewable energy, grid infrastructure or power generation is desirable.

• Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance, is strongly preferred.

• Strong writing, coordination, consultation and capacity-building skills in multicultural settings.

8. Duration and Location

• Duration: Part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and GFPP availability.

• Location: Remote-based, with regular travel to project sites on Vanua Levu, Taveuni and other islands as required for scoping, consultation and supervision.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY CYBERSECURITY LEVEL PROTECTION ASSESSMENT SERVICE AND COMMERCIAL CRYPTOGRAPHY APPLICATION SECURITY EVALUATION SERVICE

for 

China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

Country: People's Republic of China

Name of Project: China Food Safety Improvement Project

Loan No.: IBRD-92130

Assignment Title: Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package II (Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Service and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Evaluation Service)

Reference No.:  GD-FSS-GAMR-CS13

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 0.56 million.

(I) Scope of Service

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Contents

1. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services

Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

2. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

(III) Service Period

The service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029). The specific service timeline will be implemented in phases based on the system launch schedule of the four informatization projects.

(IV) Deliverables

The deliverables required for this project are as follows:

No.

Report

Submission Date/Phase

1

Mobilization Report

TERM OF REFERENCE

To ensure the implementation of the World Bank China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package II (Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Service and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Evaluation Service) of the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulationand to guarantee the achievement of the project's objectives, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select a service agency through procurement to be responsible for the implementation of this project.

 

I. Background and Description

The World Bank Loan China Food Safety Demonstration Project officially entered into force on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period until March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety at both national and local levels. As a key implementer of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of 10 million US dollars and will precisely support the achievement of the project goals through the construction of six core sub-projects:

i. Develop a full-chain traceability platform for "coding, tracing, and recalling" food in key areas, enabling whole-process traceability and risk early warning with 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

ii. Build the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" system under the Guangdong Food Safety initiative, covering intelligent video supervision of scenarios such as elderly care and campus canteens;

iii. Upgrade and transform the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and improve the accident emergency response mechanism;

iv. Carry out a capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of skill competitions;

v. Establish a high-quality food standard system and conduct promotion activities, developing no less than 30 standards and carrying out quality monitoring within two years;

vi. Provide professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above-mentioned construction content, we plan to refer to advanced practices from other World Bank projects to further optimize procurement management and improve service coordination efficiency; in the next phase of actual procurement operations, while keeping the total project budget unchanged, we intend to integrate the network security level protection assessment services and commercial cryptography application security assessment services for these 4 projects—the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Areas (or Key Varieties), the Guangdong Food Safety "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" System Construction Project, the Emergency Real-Time Dispatching and Command System Upgrade, Transformation, and Operation Project, and the Capacity Improvement Project for Food-Related Personnel in the Market Supervision Field—into a single package for unified procurement and management, so as to ensure the smooth achievement of the project's construction goals.

 

II. Objectives

The core objective of this project is to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety. Through the in-depth integration and linkage of the "Code Tracing" full-chain traceability platform, the "Internet + Smart Kitchen & Bright Stove" intelligent supervision system, and the emergency real-time dispatch and command system, a full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early warning response, and closed-loop disposal will be established, providing a data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating result indicators such as the "proportion of early warnings for which mitigation measures have been initiated." Additionally, the food-related personnel capacity improvement learning and assessment system will enable systematic training for regulatory personnel and quantify the participation proportion of female regulatory personnel.

The core purpose is to conduct a comprehensive and objective security assessment of the above-mentioned information systems in accordance with relevant national standards and norms, accurately identify and locate risks and weaknesses in the systems' network security and cryptographic applications, and propose targeted rectification suggestions accordingly. Through the approach of "promoting construction through assessment, promoting reform through assessment, and promoting application through assessment," it will ultimately ensure that all information systems meet the requirements of compliance, correctness, and effectiveness in terms of network security protection and cryptographic applications. This will provide a solid guarantee for the smooth acceptance and safe operation of the project, ensure that the collection, accounting, and reporting of all indicator data comply with World Bank norms, and help promote the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

 

III. Service Overview

The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 0.56 million.

(I) Scope of Services

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Content

a. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services
Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

 

b. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

ANNEX: DETAILED TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR)

TERMS OF REFERENCE

In order to ensure the effective implementation of PackageThird-Party Informatization Services (‌Special Security Evaluation and Acceptance Evaluation Services) under the above-mentioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Improvement Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to apply for a World Bank loan of USD10,000,000. It will provide targeted support for the achievement of project objectives through the implementation of six core sub-projects, as detailed below:

First, develop a full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su" for food in key sectors, which consists of 15 functional modules and 359 functional points to realize whole-process traceability and risk early warning.

Second, build the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen" of Guangdong Food Safety to realize intelligent video supervision covering canteens of elderly care institutions, campuses and other scenarios.

Third, upgrade and renovate the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and improve the emergency response mechanism for food safety incidents.

Fourth, launch a capacity improvement program for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of professional skills competitions.

Fifth, establish and promote a high-quality food standard system, develop no fewer than 30 standards within two years, and carry out corresponding quality monitoring work.

Sixth, provide full-process professional consulting services for project implementation.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above contents, relevant practices of other World Bank projects will be referenced to optimize procurement management and enhance the overall efficiency of service coordination. In the subsequent actual procurement process and without changing the total project budget, the special security evaluation and acceptance evaluation services of four sub-projects - namely, the full-chain food traceability platform project with“ShangMa Su”for key food sectors (categories), the Guangdong Food Safety “Internet-based Visualization Kitchen” system construction project, the upgrading, renovation and operation project of the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and the capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field - will be integrated into one single packaged project, so as to guarantee the smooth achievement of project objectives.

2.Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of comprehensively improving the modern governance capacity of food safety, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel in the market supervision field. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as“proportion of early-warnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". Meanwhile, the learning and assessment system for capacity improvement program for food-related personnel enables systematic training for supervisors and quantifies the participation rate of female supervisor.

The core objectives are to carry out the non-destructive security evaluation by adopting methods such as simulated hacker attacks before system launch to comprehensively assess the protection capabilities of network, host, application and other layers, so as to ensure compliance with industrial safety management and control requirements and protect the security of sensitive information and public privacy; conduct multi-dimensional evaluation and compliance inspection covering functionality, performance, information security and compatibility before final project acceptance to strictly control project quality, so as to ensure that all indicators fully comply with the contract, requirement specification and construction specifications. This provides a solid guarantee for the smooth acceptance and safe operation of the project, ensures the collection, accounting and reporting of all indicator data conform to World Bank standards, and facilitates the efficient implementation of the World Bank project.

3. Scope of Services

Total investment for this project amounts to RMB 420,000.

3.1 Scope of Service Recipients

The scope of services of this project covers special security evaluation services and acceptance evaluation services for four information-based sub-projects, specifically as follows:

1.Full-chain food traceability platform project with "ShangMa Su" for key food sectors (categories);

2.Guangdong Food Safety "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen" system construction project;

3.Upgrading, renovation and operation project of the real-time emergency dispatching command system;

4.Capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field.

3.2 Service Content

3.2.1 Special Security Evaluation Service

Before the system launch on the Guangdong E-Government Cloud or domestic cloud, the service provider shall conduct a pre-launch security evaluation of the system. The security evaluation institution shall conduct non-destructive penetration testing on the system by simulating hacker attack methods. The objective is to attempt system intrusion and obtain system control privileges, and deliver a report to the Client documenting the intrusion process and details. The evaluation shall focus on networks, hosts, applications, data and the overall system, to assess whether the system has adequate capabilities of information security protection, meets the safety management and control requirements of the industry and competent authorities, can continuously provide secure, stable and efficient business support, and can safeguard sensitive information and public privacy.

3.2.2 Acceptance Evaluation Services

Before the final project acceptance, the service provider shall conduct pre-acceptance evaluation and compliance inspection for the informatization service project to strictly control project quality, so as to ensure that all indicators fully comply with the contract, requirement specification and construction specifications. The scope mainly includes functional testing, performance efficiency testing, information security testing, compatibility testing, reliability testing, usability testing, maintainability testing, portability testing, and documentation review, among others.

3.3 Service Period

The service period shall commence on the date of contract signing and end on the project closure date (March 31, 2029). The specific service schedule shall be implemented in phases in accordance with the system launch and acceptance progress of the four informatization sub-projects.

4.Deliverables, Review and Acceptance

4.1 Deliverables

4.2 Deliverable Review and Acceptance

After the Project Office reviews and approves submitted deliverable reports, the service provider shall cooperate with the Project Office to submit documents required for World Bank review, and the stage deliverables shall only be formally finalized upon receiving a no-objection opinion from the World Bank. All deliverables shall fully comply with the service requirements specified in this TOR, with standardized format, complete content and authentic, accurate data.

5.Institutional and Personnel Qualification Requirements

5.1 Institutional Qualifications

5.1.1 Qualification Requirements for the Service Provider

The service provider undertaking both special security evaluation and acceptance evaluation services shall hold valid qualifications: either the Certificates of Accreditation for Testing Laboratories (including CNAS Laboratory Accreditation Certificates) issued by the China National Accreditation Service for Conformity Assessment (CNAS), or the Certificate of Metrology Accreditation (CMA) issued by market supervision authorities at or above the provincial level. The service provider shall have independently completed no fewer than 5 projects of special security evaluation and acceptance evaluation services within the past three years. Such track records shall cover government informatization, software platform development, system integration, cybersecurity and other relevant categories, which can fully demonstrate the provider’s comprehensive service capacity to conduct pre-launch security evaluation and final quality control for complex informatization projects.

5.2 Personnel Qualifications

To ensure the quality of the special security evaluation service and acceptance evaluation service under this project, a dedicated service team shall be assigned. I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

IV. DELIVERABLES

The Consultant shall deliver the following key deliverables during the implementation of the Assignment.

Deliverable 1. Inception Report

Within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date of the Contract, the Consultant shall submit a Draft Inception Report, including:

  • work plan and timeline;
  • expert mobilisation plan;
  • risk assessment and mitigation measures;
  • Quality Assurance Plan.

Deliverable 2. Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 20 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

 

Deliverable 3. Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs

The following outputs shall be produced under Deliverable 2:

  • 21 drafts of specialised model programs developed and obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities.

Deliverable 4. Final Completion Report

The following outputs shall be delivered under this deliverable and documented in the Final Completion Report:

  • full package with forty-one (41) final approved programs;
  • documentation of the development process and quality assurance activities;
  • lessons learned and next steps for further implementation.

The Consultant shall submit a Draft Final Completion Report no later than one month before the completion of the Assignment, summarising overall implementation results, achievement of objectives and targets, key lessons learned, and recommendations for further institutionalisation and sustainability.

Reports Submission and Acceptance Procedure

The following procedure shall apply to all reports submitted under this Assignment: the Inception Report (Deliverable 1), Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 2), and Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 3) and the Final Completion Report (Deliverable 4).

The exact format of the reports will be discussed and agreed upon with MoES and, where applicable, with the World Bank, upon contract signing and before the commencement of the Assignment. All reports and deliverables will be submitted in a minimum of two (2) hard copies in English and two (2) hard copies in Ukrainian. The products developed (model programs as well as methodological materials for development for Ukrainian-speaking users) shall be submitted in Ukrainian only, without translation, and included as annexes to the relevant reports. All materials developed under this Assignment shall become the property of MoES.

The Consultant shall submit:

  • the draft version of the Inception Report – within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs  – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of the Final Report – at latest 30 calendar days before the completion of the services.

The draft of each report shall be submitted in electronic (Word/Excel and PDF) format to the Client’s email address specified in the Contract. The Client will review the draft within 14 calendar days from the date of receipt and provide comments, or confirm the quality and correspondence of the Assignment with the requirements of these Terms of Reference. The Consultant, within 7 calendar days from receipt of comments, shall process them and submit the revised report in electronic and paper format, together with a table indicating, for each comment, the method of its consideration or justification for any deviation.

If the Client has no comments on the revised report, the report shall be deemed approved, which shall be confirmed by a signed Acceptance Certificate for Services. If the Client does not respond with comments within the above-mentioned period, the draft report shall be deemed accepted.

If required by MoES, the Consultant shall provide ad-hoc reports within 3–7 calendar days, depending on the complexity of the request.

V. REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Consultant

The Consultant must be a legally registered firm or a Joint Venture / Consortium of firms.

Minimum Qualification Requirements (Pass/Fail Basis)

Failure to meet any of the requirements below shall result in disqualification.

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 3 (three) years of experience in education, curriculum development, institutional development, or related fields;
  • At least 3 (three) successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:

–       curriculum development or educational program design;

–       vocational education or education sector projects;

–       capacity building programs for education institutions.

In case of a Joint Venture / Consortium (JVCA), the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least 3 (three) years of relevant experience and participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments. The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial Capacity

  • Average annual turnover for the last 3 completed financial years shall be at least USD 150,000 or equivalent.

 In case of a JVCA: Lead Member: minimum 50% of the annual turnover requirement; Other members: minimum 25% of the annual turnover requirement; Combined: must fully meet the annual turnover requirement. Audited financial statements or verified financial documents shall be provided.

Experience with Donor-Funded Projects

  • At least one assignment financed by international financial institutions or bilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, EU, GIZ, UNICEF, etc.) within the last 5 years is an advantage.

5.2.1 Minimum expected staff inputs

KE4. Quality Assurance Expert

Responsibilities:

  • development and ensuring effective performance of internal quality assurance system, including design and implementation of the Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensuring consistency and compliance across all programs;

Qualifications:

  • at least a Master’s degree;
  • at least 7 years of experience in quality assurance in education;
  • minimum 10 years of teaching experience at a vocational (professional), PPHE or higher education institution;
  • demonstrated experience in curriculum validation and review processes.
  • excellent command of Ukrainian and English;
  • a PhD (or Candidate of Sciences / Doctor of Philosophy degree) in a relevant field would be considered an asset.

5.2.3 Qualifications of Non Key experts

In addition to the Key Experts, the Consultant will engage Non-Key Experts for the proper implementation of the Assignment. for the development, review, and finalisation of model programs.

Qualifications:

  • Master's degree (minimum) in the relevant subject area; PhD is an advantage;
  • at least 5 years of teaching or subject-matter experience at vocational (professional), PPHE, or higher education institutions;
  • proven experience in curriculum or educational content development;
  • knowledge of national education standards and professional standards in the relevant sector;
  • fluent command of the Ukrainian language; working knowledge of English is an advantage.

The Consultant shall ensure that all Non-Key Experts possess qualifications and experience relevant to the tasks assigned to them under the Assignment.

The involvement, number, profile and level of effort of Non-Key Experts shall be proposed by the Consultant in the technical proposal and further specified in the Inception Report and staffing plan. The MOES approval to a proposed Non-Key Expert shall be obtained prior to mobilisation based on a curriculum vitae supplied by the Consultant.

5.2.4 Supporting Staff

The Consultant shall provide adequate supporting staff (editor, administrative assistant, financial assistant) needed to support the expert team throughout the Assignment.

Supporting staff shall meet the following minimum requirements:

  • higher education relevant to the respective function (e.g., philology/linguistics for editors, finance/accounting for the financial assistant, administration/office management for the administrative assistant);
  • at least 3 years of general working experience in the relevant field;
  • fluent command of the Ukrainian language (written and spoken); knowledge of English is an advantage for roles involving communication with international stakeholders.

VI. IMPLEMENTATION ARRANGEMENTS

The Client shall be responsible for the implementation of the overall Project and the Consultant’s Assignment shall be managed and monitored by the Client’s Implementation Group.

The Consultant shall:

  • provide all technical, organisational and administrative support;
  • ensure availability of experts according to the work plan;
  • manage team performance and delivery quality;
  • ensure compliance with timelines and deliverables.

MoES shall:

  • provide regulatory framework and templates;
  • review and approve deliverables;
  • facilitate coordination with stakeholders.

All materials developed under this Assignment shall become the property of MoES.

VII. PAYMENT SCHEDULE

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) PROGRAM

Grant number:    IDA-E0780

Job title: SRSEI Project Coordinator

Reference Number: MZ-PMU-561409-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve accountability for day-to-day implementation oversight of assigned PIU activities in the designated province(s), serving as the primary operational interface between field execution and the PCU. The PIU Coordinator will ensure that all components are effectively executed, and in a timely manner in accordance with the implementation plan.

The Project Coordinator will be required to work in close liaison with the PCU, ANE, INATRO and other stakeholders and in accordance with the Legal Agreements, and various approved project implementation manuals. A high degree of initiative and a pro-active and consultative approach will be required from the Project Coordinator in order to achieve the outcomes of this assignment. The expected duration of the assignment is 24 months. There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The Project Coordinator is required to report to the Portfolio Coordinator at the CPU of the MTL

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work; (ii) a cover letter, no more than two pages long, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The Project Coordinator should have the following minimum qualifications and skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field. 
  • At least Fifteen (15) years general working experience, of which least 10 years of progressive experience in civil works project management specifically for roads of at least 50 km or other infrastructure of similar complexity to the program
  • Experience in contract administration and management of consultants/contractors, including tracking deliverables, reviewing outputs, facilitating acceptance, and supporting invoice certification processes.
  • Experience  in contract management based on FIDIC, including prevention and/or mitigation of claims that involve financial losses to the Employer.
  • Knowledge of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), in particular ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, and ESS5..
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or coordinate teams and to work effectively with government counterparts at central and provincial levels, private sector, communities and other stakeholders.
  • Working experience in Mozambique.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken)

Desirable requirements

  • Master degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field.
  • Familiarity with OPBRC and/or Design Build contract structures.
  • Familiarity with the latest project management techniques and tools is essential. Having professional accreditation for Project Management from a recognized body.
  • Proven experience coordinating procurement processes and supporting preparation of TORs/specifications/bidding documents, and following procurement steps through contract award.
  • Demonstrated experience in GBV/SEA/SH-sensitive programme environments.
  • Good knowledge of BOQ interpretation, Detailing, Specifications, Public Procurement, Project/Contract management, Quality Control and dispute resolution.
  • Experience in the road safety standards.
  • Familiarity with national policies, procedures, and government processes.
  • Experience coordinating field implementation and undertaking regular site visits, including documenting progress, risks, quality and safeguards issues.
  • Familiarity with STEP (World Bank's procurement tracking platform) and experience with e-SISTAFE or equivalent government financial management systems.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in English must be sent in writing to the address below (only by e-mail) up to 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Attention: Portfolio Coordinator

Avenue: Martires of Inhaminga nr 336, floor 1st

Email:  procurement.ucp@mtl.gov.mz

Maputo – Mozambique

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant number:    IDA-E4810

Job title: Senior Economist

Reference Number: MZ-MTL-564463-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve provision of high-level economic and financial advisory services to the PMU and the Ministry of Transport and Logistics. The core objective of the assignment is to strengthen the Government's capacity to assess, negotiate, and manage the economic performance of transport and logistics corridor concessions in a manner that maximises sovereign value capture, ensures macro-fiscal sustainability, and aligns with international standards of regulatory best practice.

The Senior Economist will engage the National Institute of Statistics (INE) to prepare the future transport and logistic satellite account to capture regularly the contribution of the sector in the gross domestic product (GDP). There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The SE will report directly to the Project Coordinator.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work and (ii) a cover letter, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The criteria for selecting the consultant are:

a) A Master's degree or higher in Economics, Finance, Business Administration, International Banking, or a related discipline from a recognised university.

b) A minimum of 15 years of progressive professional experience in economics, finance, investment banking, or financial advisory roles, with demonstrated exposure to capital markets, regulatory environments, and financial governance at a senior level.

c) Demonstrated expertise in macroeconomic and financial modelling, with ability to develop quantitative analyses of corridor economics, concession financial structures, and fiscal risk.

d) Strong understanding of regulatory frameworks governing infrastructure concessions and public-private partnerships, as well as familiarity with prudential and fiscal governance frameworks applicable to government-held infrastructure assets.

e) Familiarity with World Bank operational procedures, including guidelines applicable to advisory and analytical assignments under Investment Project Financing.

f) Knowledge of the economic and institutional context of Mozambique, including the transport sector, public finance framework, and macroeconomic environment

g) Fluency in English is required, as the majority of analytical outputs and development partner communications will be produced in English.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in Portuguese and English must be sent in writing to the address below (by e-mail only) by 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.
