MINISTRY OF LANDS, PUBLIC WORKS, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

STATE DEPARTMENT FOR HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Consulting Services – Firm Selection

_______________________________________________________________________­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­

COUNTRY:                                    The Republic of Kenya

PROJECT TITLE:                       Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II)

PROJECT ID:                                P177048                                                       

CREDIT NO.:                               7349-KE; 7350-KE; IDA Grant Number E208-KE

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:             Consulting Services for the Preparation of Municipal Investment Opportunity Packages and Investment Readiness Support for Kisumu, Eldoret, Meru, Ruiru and Kakuma Municipalities in Kenya

CONTRACT NO.:                        KE-MOTI-566726-CS-QCBS

1.The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank (the Bank) towards the cost of the Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2.The aim of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to prepare Municipal Investment Opportunity Packages for each municipality that can attract private sector participation and improve urban service delivery and local economic development. The Consulting Services is expected to be for a period of eight (8) calendar months from the date of contract commencement.

3.The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR’s) for the assignment can be found at the following websites – www.housingandurban.go.ke and www.kusp.go.ke or can be obtained at the address given below;

4.The State Department for Housing and Urban Development (the Client) in the Ministry of Lands, Public Works, Housing and Urban Development – now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services; Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and experience to perform the services (attach evidence). The shortlisting criteria are:

a. Core business and years in business: The firm shall be duly registered/incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in the fields of municipal and urban infrastructure advisory, infrastructure finance, investment facilitation, project preparation, and/or private sector participation in urban development and service delivery. The firm shall demonstrate experience in undertaking municipal investment diagnostics, identifying and prioritizing investment opportunities, conducting pre-feasibility assessments, preparing investment opportunity packages, and strengthening institutional investment readiness for a minimum period of fifteen (15) years.

b. Must have relevant experience: The firm shall demonstrate having successfully executed and completed at least two (2) assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity within the last ten (10) years. The assignments should demonstrate experience in: (i) undertaking municipal or urban economic and investment diagnostics; (ii) identifying and prioritizing viable investment opportunities in urban infrastructure and service delivery; (iii) conducting technical, financial, institutional, environmental, and social pre-feasibility assessments; (iv) preparing investment opportunity packages; and (v) supporting investment readiness, structured private sector engagement, or investment facilitation for counties, or urban areas.

Details of similar assignments—including the name and address of the client, scope of services, contract value, implementation period, and key outputs/deliverables—should be provided in the submitted Expression of Interest (EOI), together with a clear description of the relevance of the assignments to the scope of this consultancy.

c. Technical and managerial capability of the firm: The firm shall demonstrate as having the requisite technical and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment in the submitted company profile(s).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of Consultants’ is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fourth Edition November 2020 (Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.The Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Quality Cost Based Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

7. Further information can be obtained at the address given below from 0900hrs to 1700hrs East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300hrs-1400hrs) and public holidays.

8. Expression of interest should be delivered by Tuesday 6th October 2026 at 1000hrs EAT using one of the following modalities:

a. Deposit in the Tender Box located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya;

b. Send via email to; kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke .

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form to either the tender box located at located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya or e-mail: kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke  and clearly marked with the Assignment Title and Contract Number as indicated above and addressed to:

Address:

Principal Secretary

State Department for Housing and Urban Development

Ardhi House, 6th Floor

Ngong Road

P.O. Box 30119-00100

Nairobi, Kenya

data.notice_text:
State Department for Agriculture

Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

               

                         NAIROBI

 

 

                                                                                                            

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES-INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

Country:                     Kenya

Name of project:       Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP)

Project No:                 P177816

Credit No.:                 7328-KE, 7327-KE

 

Assignment Title:      Prioritization of high-impact, transformative investments to sustainably boost  agricultural productivity and commercialization in Kenya's northern and arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL) counties - Individual selection

Reference No.          KE-MOALF-569681-CS-INDV

                                                                                                               

  1. The Government of Kenya has received a Credit from World Bank towards the cost of the Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Prioritization of high-impact, transformative investments to sustainably boost agricultural productivity and commercialization in Kenya's northern and arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL) counties.
  2. The consulting services (“Services”) main objective of the assignment is to identify, rigorously assess, and prioritize a pipeline of transformative agricultural investments capable of sustainably increasing agricultural productivity and commercialization in the target counties while maximizing economic returns, climate resilience, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and investment readiness for public, private, and development partner financing.
  3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignments can be found in the following website: www.kilimo.go.ke
  4. The Services Contracts are expected to be for a period of One Eighty (180 days).
  5. The State Department for Agriculture (the “Client”) through the Food Systems Resilience Project now invites eligible individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested individuals MUST provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, professional qualifications. The shortlisting criteria are;
    • A Master's degree in Agricultural Economics, Development Economics, Agricultural Development, International Development, Rural Development, or another closely related discipline.
    • A minimum of 10 years’ general experience of progressively responsible professional experience in agricultural transformation, investment planning, food systems development, climate-resilient agriculture, or rural development is required.
    • At least 3 years’ specific experience in designing, evaluating, and prioritizing large-scale agricultural investment programmes, particularly within Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs) or comparable dryland environments and successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar scope and complexity within the last ten (10) years. Experience on assignments financed by the World Bank, other Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs), bilateral development partners, or national governments will be an added advantage.
    • Demonstrated experience working with national governments, county governments, regional organizations, development partners, and private sector stakeholders.                                            iTechnical Competencies

The Individual Consultant shall demonstrate proven expertise in:

  • Agricultural economics, agricultural transformation, and strategic investment planning.
  • Economic and financial appraisal of investments, including cost-benefit analysis, Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR).
  • Investment prioritization using evidence-based analytical approaches, including Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA).
  • Climate-smart agriculture, sustainable agricultural development, and resilience-building in Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs).
  • Preparation of investment strategies and implementation roadmaps to support public investment planning and resource mobilization.
  • Stakeholder engagement and facilitation, including consultations with national and county governments, the private sector, development partners, and farming communities.
  • Preparation of high-quality analytical reports, policy briefs, and strategic recommendations to support government decision-making.         ii.Leadership and Coordination Capacity

The Individual Consultant shall demonstrate the ability to:

  • Lead complex multidisciplinary assignments involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Coordinate technical inputs from Government ministries, county governments, development partners, research institutions, and private sector actors.
  • Facilitate high-level policy dialogue, stakeholder consultations, and validation workshops.
  • Produce high-quality analytical reports, investment prospectuses, policy briefs, presentations, GIS products, and other decision-support materials suitable for senior government officials and development partners.      6.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised 4th Edition November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.                                            7.An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.                                                                                       8.Further information can be obtained from FSRP Procurement Offices during official working hours from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours EAT) and public holidays.                                                          9.Expressions of interest MUST be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 6th October, 2026 at 1100 hours EAT and be deposited in the tender box clearly marked State Department for Agriculture located at Kilimo house main reception Ground floor, Cathedral Road Nairobi, or send by email to: info@fsrp.go.ke and quote the Assignment title and Contract No. KE-MOALF-569681-CS-INDV in the subject row

  1. A minimum of a Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, or another relevant quantitative field from a recognized institution.
  2. At least five (5) years of demonstrable general professional experience in managing and analysing large institutional datasets, developing statistical models, and applying statistical analysis and data-mining techniques.
  3.   1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in systems analysis, business-process analysis or information systems implementation.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in requirements engineering, business-process modelling, functional specifications, systems integration analysis, system testing, user acceptance testing and requirements traceability.

    iii. KE-MOALF-571591-CS-INDV; Learning Designer Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Communication, Instructional Design, Learning Design, Educational Technology, E-Learning, Curriculum Development, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in learning design, instructional design, curriculum/content development or digital learning.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in digital learning design, instructional content development, storyboarding, assessment design, learner engagement, e-learning development and learning evaluation.

              iv. KE-MOALF-571593-CS-INDV; Webmaster Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Web Development, Digital Media, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in website administration and web operations.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in CMS administration, website maintenance, web security, backups and restoration, performance optimization, web analytics, accessibility and content publishing.

             v. KE-MOALF-571594-CS-INDV; User Interface Developer       

  1.  A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in user interface/front-end development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in responsive web/mobile interfaces, reusable components, API integration, accessibility, usability, cross-browser/device testing and interface performance optimization.

vi. KE-MOALF-571595-CS-INDV; Backend developer expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in backend/software development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in server-side application development, RESTful APIs, systems integration, secure coding, database-backed services, automated testing, performance optimization and production deployments.

  1. The Government of Kenya has received a Credit from World Bank towards the cost of the Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services as indicated above.
  2. The consulting services (“Services”) main objective of the assignment is to strengthen the Agricultural Information Resource Centre (AIRC) capacity as it transforms into the Kenya Agricultural Digital Information Centre (KADIC) to generate, manage, analyze, and translate agricultural data into timely, reliable, and actionable information that supports evidence-based decision-making, digital agricultural services, and improved agricultural productivity.
  3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignments can be found in the following website: www.kilimo.go.ke.
  4. The consultant shall be contracted for an initial period of twenty-four (24) calendar months from the contract commencement date. This period is subject to extension up to the project closing date, based on project needs, availability of funds, and satisfactory performance.
  5. The State Department for Agriculture (the “Client”) through the Food Systems Resilience Project now invites eligible individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested individuals MUST provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, professional qualifications.

The shortlisting criteria are as follows;

i)  KE-MOALF- 569688-CS-INDV-Data Science expert 1 and KE-MOALF-570715-CS- INDV- Data Science expert 2

  1. A minimum of a Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, or another relevant quantitative field from a recognized institution.
  2. At least five (5) years of demonstrable general professional experience in managing and analysing large institutional datasets, developing statistical models, and applying statistical analysis and data-mining techniques.
  3. At least three (3) years of demonstrable specific professional experience in the use of statistical and data-mining tools and techniques, database querying and management, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), distributed data-processing systems, and High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments.

ii.  KE-MOALF-571589-CS-INDV; System Analyst

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in systems analysis, business-process analysis or information systems implementation.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in requirements engineering, business-process modelling, functional specifications, systems integration analysis, system testing, user acceptance testing and requirements traceability.

    iii. KE-MOALF-571591-CS-INDV; Learning Designer Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Communication, Instructional Design, Learning Design, Educational Technology, E-Learning, Curriculum Development, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in learning design, instructional design, curriculum/content development or digital learning.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in digital learning design, instructional content development, storyboarding, assessment design, learner engagement, e-learning development and learning evaluation.

      iv. KE-MOALF-571593-CS-INDV; Webmaster Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Web Development, Digital Media, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in website administration and web operations.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in CMS administration, website maintenance, web security, backups and restoration, performance optimization, web analytics, accessibility and content publishing.

       v. KE-MOALF-571594-CS-INDV; User Interface Developer       

  1.  A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in user interface/front-end development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in responsive web/mobile interfaces, reusable components, API integration, accessibility, usability, cross-browser/device testing and interface performance optimization.

vi. KE-MOALF-571595-CS-INDV; Backend developer expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in backend/software development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in server-side application development, RESTful APIs, systems integration, secure coding, database-backed services, automated testing, performance optimization and production deployments.

     vii. KE-MOALF-571596-CS-INDV; Database Administrator

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Database Administration, Software Engineering, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in database administration and management.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in enterprise database administration, database performance tuning, backup and recovery, database security and access management, high availability, database monitoring and database lifecycle management.                     6.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised 4th Edition November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.                                                 7. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.                                                                                                  8. Further information can be obtained from FSRP Procurement offices during official working hours from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours EAT) and public holidays.                                                             9. Expressions of interest MUST be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 6th October, 2026 at 1100 hours EAT and be deposited in the tender box clearly marked State Department for Agriculture located at Kilimo house main reception Ground floor, Cathedral Road Nairobi, or send by email to: info@fsrp.go.ke and quote the Assignment title and respective Contract No.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

GREEN, AGRI-FOOD TRANSFORMATION FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY (GATE)

Reference :             GC3C1e

Assignment Title:      Integrated Capacity-Building Program on Climate-Smart Agriculture, Digital Extension, and Food Safety Services under GATE

 

The Republic of Lebanon (the “Borrower”) represented by the Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) (the “Client”) as a representative to the Borrower will implement the Green, Agri-food Transformation for Economic Recovery (the “GATE” or “Project”), funded by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (the “IBRD” or the “World Bank” or the “Bank”). The total Project cost is Two Hundred Million United States Dollars (US$ 200,000,000).

The CDR intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under a consulting services contract for the Preparation and Implementation of “Integrated Capacity-Building Program on Climate-Smart Agriculture, Digital Extension, and Food Safety Services under GATE (GC3C1e)”.

The full Terms of References (TOR) version can be found on CDR website www.cdr.gov.lb, click on the Procurement tag for more info.

The Main objective of this assignment is to strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Agriculture’s extension and rural development services, and strengthen market-oriented capacities of farmers and farmers’ groups, support farmers, farmers’ groups, and agricultural cooperatives, including beneficiaries of Climate-Smart Matching Grants under GATE Subcomponent 1.1, to adopt the technical, quality, and organizational practices needed to meet the specifications and standards of off-takers and target markets (target to be agreed).

The Consultant shall provide the Employer the main services and tasks as detailed in the provided TOR:

The time for completion of the Contract (GC3C1e) is: 18 months

The CDR now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.), in a responsive way to the below noted requirements.

In addition, interested consultants are requested to provide the following information, in a binder, and in the same order as listed below, and shall use and fill-in the attached Consultant Information Form, and submit it in one hard copy and one editable (Excel or Word format) soft copy in:

  • A duly completed Cover Letter stating the interest of the applicant in providing the mentioned services.
  • A concise presentation of the firm(s) (brochures, statements of type, property and key tasks etc.).
  • List of ONLY relevant similar projects (maximum 10 projects) as defined in the Terms of References, ongoing and/or completed within the last 10 years, indicating the provided services, the percentage of participation in JV (if any), and the size/value of relevant contracts (in USD and in person-month).
  • Detailed descriptions of two (2) handled completed projects within the last ten (10) years that demonstrate experience in providing services similar in nature, scope and complexity to the proposed assignment, as defined in the Terms of References. Only projects completed within the last ten (10) years shall be considered.
  • Overall firm's employees list and personnel availability and structure (list, number, organization structure, etc… of the core, backstopping and supporting staff).
  • Experience in Lebanon and/or the Middle East.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025”, which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with another firm in the form of a "Joint Venture" to enhance their qualifications, name and nationality of the partner in charge shall be specified. All members should have well defined inputs to the assignment, and shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire consultant's obligations under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Eligible firms, which have submitted the necessary statements in a satisfactory responsive way, might be short listed.

The shortlisting criteria for firms interested in providing these services include:

  • Core Business and Years of Experience: The firm should have at least 10 years of experience in preparing and delivering agricultural extension, food safety systems and capacity-building programs, including those funded by the World Bank or other development finance institutions (DFIs).
  • Relevant Project Experience: The firm should demonstrate a successful track record in preparing and delivering climate-smart training, and participatory field-based learning, food safety systems and capacity-building programs.
  • Technical and Managerial Capacity: The firm should have a proven capacity to manage complex, multidisciplinary teams and to deliver projects meeting international standards, especially regarding technical quality, cost control, scheduling, risk management including environmental and social risks.

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (from 09:00 to 14:00 Beirut local Time).

Expressions of Interest must be delivered to the address below by hand or carrier including one original, one hard copy and one electronic CD ROM, not later than 12:00 noon, Beirut local time on Tuesday, October 6th, 2026, mentioning as reference:

" Integrated Capacity-Building Program on Climate-Smart Agriculture, Digital Extension, and Food Safety Services under GATE (GC3C1e)"

Country: Independent State of Papua New Guinea (PNG)

Name of Project: PNG Resilient Transport Project (RTP)

Contract Title: Firm for undertaking Bridge Investigation, Design and Contract Documentation – Ramu Highway – Morobe and Madang Provinces

Credit No.: Finance/Loan/Grant Nos.: 7091PG / 9379PG

DoWH Reference Number: PG-DOW-555092-CS-QCBS

NPC Reference Number: NPC/2026-39

  1. The Independent State of Papua New Guinea has received financing from the World Bank towards the implementation of a PNG Resilient Transport Project (RTP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. Department of Works and Highways (DoWH) is the Implementing Agency (IA) and has established a Project Implementing Unit (PIU), which is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of the Project.
  2. The DoWH now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
  3. Details regarding the assignment, duration, tasks, and responsibilities etc. are mentioned in the detailed EoI and ToR which can be obtained from the undersigned.
  4. The shortlisting criteria are:
    1. Core business (feasibility studies, surveys etc.) with at least seven years in business;
    2. Experience in similar projects of comparable size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area of Bridges (feasibility studies, detailed engineering designs, environmental and social assessments, preparation of technical specifications, BOQ, drafting bid documents etc.)
    3. Financial Soundness of the Firm (minimum average annual turnover of US$ 5 million)
    4. Technical and managerial organization of the firm.
    5. Familiarity with business operations in Papua New Guinea (desirable).

Note:

      1. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
      2. When providing information relating to (b), it shall be made clear whether the experience of the firm was in the capacity of a principal firm (lead partner) or as an associated firm (sub-consultant/JV partner) with detail regarding the scope of the services.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.
  4. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method as set out in Section VII, paragraph 7.3 of World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition (September 2025, effective 1 September, 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

data.notice_text:
COUNTRY: Republic of Mozambique

NAME OF PROJECT: Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant No.: IDA-E4810

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Supervision of Civil Works to Improve Road Safety at Schools and locations along the Nacala Corridor with iRAP Less Than Three Stars

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): 45A000141/CP/06/2026

The Government of Mozambique (GOM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards the payment for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) is to supervise the works based on FIDIC’s definition of the duties and responsibilities of the “Engineer”. The Consultant will also take the necessary measures and provide appropriate advice to the Project Implementation Unit (the PIU) to enable the construction contract to be completed in a timely and cost-effective manner, in conformity with the contract conditions and specifications. The Consultant shall develop, implement, and document a structured theoretical and on-the-job training program for two (2) graduate engineers selected by the PIU and assigned to the Project. The Consultant shall inspect and supervise any corrective repairs, the recovery of closed borrow pits or other degraded areas and other works (including the administrative aspects of the works) during the DLP. For purposes of carrying out these services, the Consultant shall assign his personnel to carry out inspection of the works and send a team of his personnel on the final inspection, preparation and issuing of the final certificate. During this period, the Consultant shall be expected to draw the attention of the contractors to any identified defects and shall supervise the subsequent remedial works by the contractor, as well as report to the PIU on defects and remedial works.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The evaluation of expressions of interest will be made on qualitative basis and the short-listing criteria are:

  1. Profile of the Firm/ Core business demonstrating roads and bridge design experience; experience in works supervision of road improvement or rehabilitation contracts;
  2. General experience of the firm (must be at least 20 years) in the field; and
  3. Description of at least five (5) similar assignments demonstrating the Consultant’s experience, with contracts in similar conditions.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain Five (5) to Eight (8) shortlisted firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained by sending an email to procurement.ucp@mtl.gov.mz during office hours 0900 to 1500 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by mail or by e-mail)” by 15hours,  6th October 2026 .

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

ANGOLA

DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL REFERENCE INSTRUMENTS FOR THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS

REFERENCE NO.:  57/CS/C2SC3.A18.3/26

The Government of the Republic of Angola received a loan of US$150 million from the World Bank (WB) and a donation of US$50 million from the Global Partnership for Education for the implementation of the Tertiary Education, Science, and Technology Project (TEST) and intends to apply part of this financing to hire a firm to provide Development of National Reference Instruments for the Digital Transformation of Higher Education Institutions.

The TEST Project aims to: (i) improve the quality of student preparation to increase total enrolment and expand opportunities for more equitable access; (ii) improve the quality and alignment of curricula with the labour market and instruction in priority training areas; and (iii) improve the governance and management of the education sector.

This consultancy aims the specialized consultancy to support MESCTI in the drafting, validation, consolidation, and preparation for institutional approval of National Reference Instruments for the Digital Transformation of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs).

The shortlisting criteria are:

The company must demonstrate that it has the following qualifications:

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project

Using the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA)

 

Loan No.: 98750-BW

 

Assignment Title: Consulting Services to Carry Out an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory (NDQCL)

Reference No.: BW-BOMRA-561248-CS

1. Background

The Republic of Botswana has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project (HEPRRP) under the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards the procurement of consulting services.

The Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA), as the implementing agency, intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to prepare an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for the proposed National Drug Quality Control Laboratory (NDQCL).

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a site-specific, practical, and implementable Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for the construction and operational phases of the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory (NDQCL), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).

3. Scope of the Services

The consulting services shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

  1. Conduct environmental and social baseline assessments.
  2. Identify and assess potential environmental and social risks and impacts associated with the proposed laboratory during construction and operation.
  3. Develop appropriate environmental and social mitigation and monitoring measures.
  4. Undertake stakeholder engagement and consultations with relevant stakeholders.
  5. Recommend institutional arrangements and capacity-building measures for effective ESMP implementation.
  6. Prepare a comprehensive Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) that complies with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), and relevant national environmental legislation.

The assignment is expected to be completed within four (4) to five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

4. Eligibility and Shortlisting Criteria

The Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

4.1 Firm Experience

The Consultant should demonstrate:

  1. A minimum of ten (10) years' experience in environmental and/or social assessment, planning and management, particularly for infrastructure and construction-related projects.
  2. Demonstrated experience in undertaking Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and preparing associated environmental and social instruments, including Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs), Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), or similar instruments.
  3. Proven experience in conducting environmental and social assessments for national governments and/or development partner-funded projects, including familiarity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
  4. Experience in climate change adaptation, disaster risk management and resilience planning.
  5. Experience in laboratory facilities, healthcare infrastructure, pharmaceutical facilities, or projects involving chemical and biological hazards within Botswana, or the Southern African region will be an added advantage.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. Conflict of Interest

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025 edition) setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

6. Association with Other Firms

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications.

7. Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualifications Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

8. Request for Further Information

Further information may be obtained during normal working hours (08:00–16:00 hours, Botswana time) at the address provided below.

9. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of Interest must be submitted in writing (by hand delivery, courier, mail or e-mail) to the address below no later than:

Tuesday 06th October 2026 at 16:00 hours (Botswana Time).

The submission should be clearly marked:

"Expression of Interest – Consulting Services to Carry Out an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory (NDQCL)"

10. Submission Address

Gaborone Station
Botswana

REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

ACCELERATING ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND JOB CREATION PROJECT

Loan No.: IBRD-95270

Project ID: P178035

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR NEEDS ASSESSMENT, TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS, AND SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED BORDER INTELLIGENCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT SOLUTION

Reference No. 98CS1/MINPLAN/26

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Needs Assessment, Technical Specifications, and Support for the Development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to provide technical support to the Coordinated Border Management Committee (CGCF) in all phases prior to and during the development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution. The role of the consulting firm includes:

  1. Identifying the functional and operational needs at the borders, mapping and reviewing existing processes, and inventorying technological systems in use;
  2. Developing the functional and technical architecture of the solution, defining interoperability requirements, creating a data dictionary and data model, and estimating the development and implementation costs;
  3. Assisting in the preparation of the bidding documents for the selection of the technology development company and issuing a substantiated technical opinion on the recommended proposal;

data.title: Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Investigations and Studies for the Design of the Mesurado Industrial Fishing Port
data.project_name: Liberia Sustainable Management of Fisheries Project
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION INTEREST (REOI)

Loan/ Credit No. IDA V3100 PROJECT ID: P172012

Subject: Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) for Provision of Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Investigations and Studies for the Design of the Mesurado Industrial Fishing Port

Reference No.: LR-NAFAA-572805-CS-CQS

The government of Liberia through the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA) has received support from the World Bank Group toward the implementation of the “Liberia Sustainable Management of Fisheries Project (LSMFP)”, and intends to utilize part of the funds for the construction of an industrial fish export terminal and an artisanal fish landing site at Mesurado Pier in Monrovia. The artisanal fisheries landing site will be equipped with post-harvest processing facilities, fish market facilities and store facilities for the sale of vessel engines and nets, engine repair shops, toilets and water supply facilities.

The Government of Liberia through NaFAA is soliciting the services of a qualified Consultant Firm or Consultant Consortia to conduct geotechnical investigations and studies for the design of the Mesurado Industrial Fishing Port. The objective of the consultancy is to contract a geotechnical firm to undertake:

1.         The 6 (six) geotechnical boreholes required;

2.         The analysis of the data from the laboratory tests;

Given the impossibility of mobilizing a jack-up barge within the timeframe of the project, it is proposed that the boreholes inside the port are carried out from a normal flat barge, whereas the boreholes on the seaside of the breakwater are carried out over the edge of the breakwater slope, using either coarse backfill or scaffolding to hold the drilling rig in place. The geotechnical investigation shall likely comprise:

•           CANOE HUB - 4 boreholes drilled over the outer slope of the lee breakwater to a depth of 20 metres below LAT level.

The National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA) now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in performing the Services. Interested firms must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (brief corporate profile: technical and managerial capability of the firm, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills and staff, etc.)

The shortlisting criteria includes the following qualifications:

Qualification Requirements and Composition of Study Team:

The Firm must show evidence of minimum ten (10) years’ general experience in geotechnical engineering, marine geotechnical investigations, and marine construction works. To demonstrate required competence and adequacy to successfully complete the assignment, the firm must have specific in-depth and recent experience in at least one similar assignment in the last 10 years.

Further, the firm should preferably be ISO 9001-2015 certified and should be able to field key professional personnel with adequate technical background, experience and capability in the field of marine engineering.

The firm must have certified access (i.e. direct ownership or a valid rental agreement) to a flat barge of the required dimensions from which to carry out the boreholes inside the port.

The materials testing laboratory to be used for the analysis of the samples shall be ISO/IEC 17025 certified and accredited by a national accreditation authority of the firm’s country of origin.

All geotechnical investigations, including borehole drilling, soil and rock sampling, Standard Penetration Testing (SPT), Cone Penetration Testing (CPT/CPTu), laboratory testing, rock coring, geological logging, groundwater monitoring, interpretation and reporting, shall be carried out in accordance with the latest applicable editions of internationally recognized standards.

The investigation shall principally comply with BS 5930:2015+A1:2020 (Code of Practice for Ground Investigations), EN 1997-1 and EN 1997-2 (Eurocode 7) for geotechnical design and ground investigation, ISO 22475-1:2021 for sampling methods and groundwater measurements, ISO 22476-1:2022 for CPT/CPTu, and ISO 22476-3:2005+A1:2011 together with ASTM D1586/D1586M and ASTM D6066/D6066M-24 for SPT execution and normalization of N values. Soil identification and classification shall conform to ISO 14688-1:2017, ISO 14688-2:2017, ASTM D2488, and ASTM D2487, while rock description and classification shall follow ISO 14689:2017. Borehole drilling and sampling shall utilize ASTM D1452/D1452M-25 for auger borings, ASTM D6151-25 for hollow-stem auger exploration, and ASTM D6914/D6914M where sonic drilling is employed. Laboratory testing shall be undertaken in accordance with the ISO 17892 series and applicable ASTM methods, including ASTM D2216 (moisture content), ASTM D4318 (Atterberg limits), ASTM D6913/D7928 (particle-size distribution), ASTM D3080 (direct shear), ASTM D4767 (consolidated triaxial testing), ASTM D2435/D2435M (consolidation), ASTM D698/D1557 (compaction), ASTM D1883 (CBR), and ASTM D7012-23 for the compressive strength and elastic properties of intact rock cores. Rock coring, core recovery, RQD determination, logging and preservation shall comply with ISO 22475-1, BS 5930, ISO 14689, and current ISRM Suggested Methods, with detailed records of core recovery, lithology, weathering, discontinuities, groundwater conditions and RQD included in the borehole logs. All laboratory analyses shall be performed by laboratories operating under ISO/IEC 17025, with documented QA/QC procedures, equipment calibration, chain-of-custody records and certified test results. Where any cited standard has been withdrawn or superseded, the Consultant shall apply the current replacement or an internationally recognized equivalent, subject to the Engineer's approval.

The firm will assemble a multi-disciplinary team of technicians which must include the key experts as stated below, though the consultant may propose additional expertise as required as non-key experts; however, their qualifications will not be considered in the evaluation of proposal. The proposed key staff listed below will not be evaluated at this stage:

                       Team Leader / Senior Marine Geotechnical Engineer pert, Senior Drilling / Geotechnical           

                        Investigation Engineer, Marine Geotechnical / Offshore Investigation Specialist,

                       Laboratory / Materials Testing Engineer, Marine HSE / Drilling Safety Specialist

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following websites:

  1. www.nafaa.gov.lr
  2. www.emansion.gov.lr
  3. https://nafaa.gov.lr/projects/lsmmfp

The attention of interested individual Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Please refer to paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations on conflict of interest related to this assignment which is available on the Bank’s website     at http://projectsbeta.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and- services/brief/procurement-newframework .

A Consultancy Firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection Method (CQS) set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1600 hours GMT.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by Wednesday October 7, 2026 @ 4:00PM GMT

Mesurado Pier, Freeport of Monrovia Monrovia, Liberia

UGP-MEAH

 

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET OUVERT NATIONAL

Date de lancement :

AMI N° 12-2026/MEAH/PAAEP/AMI

Nom du Projet : Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable

Crédit IDA N°71210

Réf. STEP : MG-MEAH-563208-CS-CQS

Intitulé : « RECRUTEMENT D’UN BUREAU D’ÉTUDES POUR LES PROJETS DE CONSTRUCTION DE LABORATOIRE ET DE REHABILITATION DE BATIMENT DU MINISTERE DE L’EAU, DE L’ASSAINISSEMENT ET DE L’HYGIENE ».

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar, par le biais du Ministère de l’Eau, de l’Assainissement et l’Hygiène, a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable (PAAEP), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat cité en objet.
  2. L’objectif général de la mission est d’assurer les études, le contrôle et la surveillance des travaux de réhabilitation des bâtiments administratifs et de construction de nouveau laboratoire du MEAH, afin de fournir des infrastructures modernes, fonctionnelles, accessibles, durables et conformes aux exigences techniques, environnementales et sociales suivants les normes nationales et internationales applicables.

La durée prévisionnelle d’exécution de l’étude est fixée à six (06) mois, et celle de la phase de contrôle est prévue de douze (12) mois. La durée réelle de cette phase sera ajustée en fonction du calendrier effectif des travaux.

  1. Les services attendus comprennent les deux (02) missions suivantes :
  • Mission 1 : Études techniques ;
  • Mission 2 : Contrôle et surveillance des travaux.
  1. L’UGP MEAH invite le Bureau d’Études éligibles à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Le Bureau d’Études ou groupements intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des prestations. Le Bureau d’Études ou groupements devront présenter un profil multidisciplinaire et justifier des compétences nécessaires à la bonne conduite de la mission.

 

  1. Profil requis :

Le Bureau d’Études devra justifier d’une expérience avérée dans la réalisation de prestations de maîtrise d’œuvre technique, notamment les études, le contrôle et la surveillance de travaux de construction de bâtiments et/ou d’ouvrages de génie civil. Il devra également disposer d’un personnel qualifié et de moyens logistiques adéquats permettant la bonne exécution de la mission.

À ce titre, le Bureau d’Études devra notamment :

  • Présenter au moins cinq (05) références pertinentes en maîtrise d’œuvre technique (études, contrôle et surveillance) pour des projets de bâtiments et/ou de génie civil ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience en maîtrise d’œuvre complète ;
  • Justifier d’au moins trois (03) expériences dans la gestion ou l’appui à la gestion des processus d’Appel d’Offres relatifs à des travaux de construction (assistance à maîtrise d’ouvrage) ;
  • Justifier d’au moins trois (03) expériences de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux, notamment dans la réalisation d’études d’impact environnemental et social et le suivi des mesures de sauvegarde ;
  • Disposer d’une expérience confirmée dans la réalisation, le contrôle ou la supervision de projets financés par la Banque Mondiale ou d’autres partenaires techniques et financiers ;
  • Mettre à disposition un personnel technique qualifié et adapté aux exigences de la mission ;
  1. Les Bureau d’Études devront présenter dans leurs dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt, les PV de réception (provisoire ou définitif) ou les certificats de bonne fin des prestations similaires pour justification. Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.
  2.  Les Bureau d’Études peuvent s'associer avec d'autres Bureau d’Études pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d'un groupement. Dans le cas d'un groupement, tous les membres du groupement seront solidairement responsables de l'ensemble du contrat, s'ils seront sélectionnés.
  3. Seuls le Bureau d’Études démontrant leur capacité à réaliser les missions susmentionnées seront invités à soumettre leurs propositions techniques et financières.
  4. Les Termes de Références (TDRs) pour la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet du projet mentionnés ci-dessous : www.paaep.mg   
  5. Les Bureau d’Études ou le groupement sera sélectionné suivant la méthode de Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications des consultants (SQC) en accord avec les procédures de la Banque Mondiale définies dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés par les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI), de la Banque mondiale en date du juillet 2016, mise à jour septembre 2023 (5ème édition).
  6. Les Bureau d’Études ou le groupement intéressé peut obtenir de plus amples informations, pendant les heures de bureau (08h 00mn à 16h 00mn heure locale), à de l’adresse : Bâtiment A1– Rez-de-chaussée. Explorer Business Park (Ex-village des jeux) Ankorondrano, Antananarivo 101, Madagascar.  
  7.  Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être remises (en personne, par courrier ou par e-mail) avec la référence de l’Appel à Manifestation d’Intérêt et la mention « RECRUTEMENT D’UN BUREAU D’ÉTUDES POUR LES PROJETS DE CONSTRUCTION DE LABORATOIRE ET DE REHABILITATION DE BATIMENT DU MINISTERE DE L’EAU, DE L’ASSAINISSEMENT ET DE L’HYGIENE » au plus tard le Mercredi 07 OCTOBRE 2026 à seize heure 16h 00mn heure locale, à l’adresse ci-après :

PROJET PAAEP – UGP MEAH

Bâtiment A1– Rez-de-chaussée. Explorer Business Park (Ex-village des jeux) Ankorondrano, Antananarivo 101, Madagascar.

Site web : www.paaep.mg

2. Danmanlk hizmetlerinin kapsam, orman yangnlarna hassas ormanlarn bulunduu Orman Bölge Müdürlüklerindeki Orman letme Müdürlüklerinin, Yangn Yönetim Planlarnn yenilenmesi ile bölgenin yangn riskinin belirlenmesi, birimlerin yangnlarn önlenmesine yönelik yangn öncesi yapaca faaliyetler ile meydana gelen orman yangnlarnda, araç ve personel kapasitesinin en verimli ekilde kullanlmasna yönelik teknik esaslar belirlemektir.  in Ekim 2026 tarihinde balamas planlanmakta olup, tamamlanma süresi 75 takvim günüdür.

 3. e ilikin ayrntl Tanm (TOR) aadaki internet adresinde bulunabilir:

Tarm ve Orman Bakanl, Orman Genel Müdürlüü / Orman Yangnlar ile Mücadele Dairesi Bakanl uygun danmanlk firmalarn (“Danmanlar”), aada ad geçen hizmetleri salamaya yönelik olarak ilgi bildiriminde bulunmaya davet etmektedir. lgilenen Danmanlarn,  hizmetleri yerine getirmek üzere istenen deneyime ve niteliklere sahip olduklarn gösteren bilgi ve belgeleri salamaldrlar.

GRUP 1 - Yangn Yönetim Plannn Hazrlanmas Hizmet Alm (Mersin Orman Bölge Müdürlüü) (Ref. No: TR-OGM-564934-CS-CQS)

GRUP 2 - Yangn Yönetim Plannn Hazrlanmas Hizmet Alm (Adana Orman Bölge Müdürlüü) (Ref. No: TR-OGM-564930-CS-CQS)

GRUP 4 - Yangn Yönetim Plannn Hazrlanmas Hizmet Alm (Kahramanmara Orman Bölge Müdürlüü) (Ref. No: TR-OGM-564913-CS-CQS)

Danmanlk Firmalar birden fazla görev için ilgi göstermilerse, yukarda belirtilen Referans Numaralarn belirterek hangi görev(ler) için ilgi gösterdiklerini bavuru yazsnda belirtmelidirler. Danmanlk Firmalarnn teklif vermek istedikleri grup / gruplar için belirttikleri oluum (tek katlm, i ortakl vs.) ayn ise; teklif verecekleri her bir paket için ayr dosya sunmalarna gerek yoktur. Orman Genel Müdürlüü, Danmanlarn hangi görev(ler) için teknik ve mali tekliflerini sunmalarnn isteneceine karar verme hakkna sahiptir.

5. Bir danmanlk firmas, görevi kendi bana yerine getirebilecek yeterlilik ve deneyime sahip olduunu deerlendiriyorsa, ilgi beyann (EOI) tek bana sunabilir. Danmanlarn, ister yerli ister yabanc olsun, baka bir firma ile ortaklk kurmalar zorunlu deildir. Bununla birlikte, danmanlar göreve ilikin niteliklerini ve kapasitelerini güçlendirmek amacyla kendi tercihleri dorultusunda bir ortaklk kurabilirler. Bu ortaklk, ya bir Ortak Giriim eklinde olabilir (bu durumda ortak giriimin tüm üyeleri mütereken ve müteselsilen sorumlu olacaktr) ya da alt danman kullanm eklinde olabilir (bu durumda danman, alt danmann salayaca hizmetler de dahil olmak üzere tüm hizmetlerden sorumlu olacaktr).

Ortaklk kurulmas halinde, danmanlarn ilgi beyan kapsamnda aadaki hususlar açklamalar gerekmektedir: a) Ortakln kurulma gerekçesi, b) Görevin yerine getirilmesindeki öngörülen rolü ve ilgili nitelikleri ile birlikte, ortak giriimin her bir üyesinin ve/veya her bir alt danmann göreve katks.  Bu açklamalarn amac, önerilen ortak giriimi üyelerinin ve/veya alt danmanlarn ortakla dahil edilmesinin gerekçelendirilmesidir. lgi beyannda yukardaki açklamalarn sunulmamas, söz konusu ortakln ksa listeye alnmamas riskini dourabilir.  Ksa liste deerlendirmesi kapsamnda, ortaklk eklinde sunulan ilgi beyanlarnn deerlendirilmesinde yalnzca ortak giriim  üyelerinin nitelikleri dikkate alnacaktr. Önerilen alt danmanlarn nitelikleri ise deerlendirmeye alnmayacaktr.

6. Aada yer alan seçim kriterleri esas alnacaktr. Bu kapsamda, danmann ihale konusu ile ilgili özel deneyimi, deerlendirmede öncelikli ve en önemli kriter olarak dikkate alnacaktr. 

  1. Danmann (firma olarak) danmanlk hizmetlerinin sunulmasna ilikin genel deneyimi: Danman, yasal olarak kurulmu ve ilgili mevzuata göre tescil edilmi ve en az be (5) yllk deneyime sahip bir danmanlk firmas olmaldr.( Ortak giriim olmas halinde, her bir ortak genel deneyim artn salamaldr.)
  2. Danmann (firma olarak) benzer büyüklükteki sözlemeler kapsamnda benzer hizmetlerin salanmasna ilikin göreve uygun özel deneyimi:Danman firmann son 10 yl içerisinde (01.01.2016 tarihinden lgi Bildirimi son bavuru tarihine kadar) yangn yönetim plan hazrlanmas, orman yangnlar risk deerlendirmesi ve planlamas, orman amenajman planlarnn hazrlanmas veya benzer nitelikteki ormanclk planlama çalmalarnda deneyim sahibi olmas beklenmektedir.

7. Yukardaki ksa liste/seçim kriterlerini karlamadaki niteliklerini ve deneyimlerini göstermek için, Danmanlardan asgari olarak aada listelenen destekleyici belgeleri sunmalar istenmektedir Bir danmanlk firmas, yeterlilik ve deneyim kriterlerini karladn yalnzca kendi kurumsal deneyimi ve nitelikleri üzerinden gösterebilir; ana irketinin, karde irketlerinin, bal ortaklklarnn veya çalanlarnn deneyim ve nitelikleri bu amaçla dikkate alnmayacaktr. 

 (i)    Firmann kurulu/ticaret/tescil belgeleri.

(ii)   Firmann temel i alanlarn içeren irket broürleri; ve

(iii)  Benzer sözlemeler hakknda bu lgi Beyan ekinde yer alan forma uygun olarak sunulan bilgiler. (En fazla 15 benzer sözleme sunulmaldr.)

(iiii)  Serbest Ormanclk irketleri, Ormanclk Kooperatifleri Orman Mühendisleri Odasndan Son Bavuru Tarihinden Önce Alnm Serbest Ormanclk / Orman Ürünleri Büro ve irketleri Oda Tescil ve 5531 Sayl Kanun’a ait Mesleki Faaliyet hale Yetkinlik Belge numarasn Yeterlik Bilgileri Tablosunda beyan etmesi ve "Serbest/Serbest Yeminli Ormanclk irketi Tescil Belgesi" veya "Serbest/Serbest Yeminli Ormanclk ve Orman Ürünleri irketi Tescil Belgesi" ilk ilan tarihinin ya da ihale veya son bavuru tarihinin içinde bulunduu ylda Orman Mühendisleri Odasndan alnm ve bu ihaleye konu i için düzenlenmi “hale yetkinlik belgesi”

8.       lgilenen Danmanlk Firmalarnn dikkati, Dünya Bankas'nn çkar çatmasna ilikin politikasn ortaya koyan, deitirilmi haliyle Kasm 2020 tarihli Dünya Bankas 'IPF Borçlular için Satn Alma Düzenlemeleri' Bölüm III, paragraf 3.14, 3.16 ve 3.17'ye çekilmektedir.

9.   Danmanlk Firmasnn seçimi, Danmanlk Klavuzunda belirtilen “Danmanlarn Niteliklerine Dayal Seçim (CQS) Yöntemi” prosedürlerine uygun olarak yaplacaktr.

10.   lgilenen firmalar yerel saatle 10.00 ile 17.00 arasndaki çalma saatlerinde, aadaki adresten daha fazla bilgi alabilir.

Reference No.: TCDRCP-C1-CS-TECHLEGAL-01.01

  1. The Urban Transformation Presidency (UTP) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Climate and Disaster Resilient Cities Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. The Consultant shall perform the assignment in accordance with the contract and its annexes and shall provide consulting services for approximately 24 months or latest until October 31, 2028, from the contract start date. All buildings shall remain under the liability of the consulting firm throughout the duration of the consulting contract and until the occupancy certificate of the buildings is obtained.
    Additionally, the general goal and intent of the consulting services ("Provision of Technical and Legal Support") are:

• To provide technical and legal support to property owners of at-risk residential and/or commercial units regarding the contracts to be signed between the property owners and contractors for the strengthening/reconstruction of such units under Component 2 of the Project.
• To conduct technical verification, supervision, monitoring, and reporting during and after the construction phase of the works carried out by contractors in close cooperation with the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change (MoEUCC) and building inspection firms, particularly in terms of quality, durability, feasibility, time, and cost, for the buildings selected through a sampling methodology by the UTP PMU.
• To fulfill all audits and tasks requested by the UTP PMU during project implementation.
• To support the UTP PMU in handling complaints.

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the services are attached to this invitation. 
  2. The detailed Terms of References (TORs) for the assignments can be found at the following web page address: https://kentseldirenclilik.csb.gov.tr/
  3. The Directorate of Urban Transformation invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
  4. A consulting firm may submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) individually if it believes it is fully capable of carrying out the assignment alone. It is not mandatory for consultants, whether foreign or local, to form a partnership with any other firm(s). Alternatively, if consultants prefer to enhance their qualifications and capacity for the assignment, such partnerships may be formed as a Joint Venture (where all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or as Sub-consultants (where the Consultant shall be responsible for the services of the sub-consultant as well). If a partnership is formed, the Consultants must explain in their EOI submission (a) the justification for forming the partnership and (b) the proposed role and qualifications of each Joint Venture member and/or sub-consultant in executing the assignment. Failure to provide this explanation in the EOI may result in the disqualification of the partnership from the shortlist. Please note that in the evaluation of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of Joint Venture members will be considered, while the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be taken into account.
  5. The selection criteria are as follows, with special emphasis on the Consultant’s specific experience related to the assignment:
  1. The Consultant (as a firm) must have at least 10 years of general experience in providing construction supervision services prior to the deadline for proposal submission. Experience in providing such services in Türkiye will be considered an asset.
  2. The Consultant (as a firm) must have specific experience in providing similar consulting services under contracts of comparable size, type, and complexity within the last ten years prior to the proposal submission deadline.

Note: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting/selection criteria, Consultants must submit at least the following supporting documents. A consulting firm can only use its own qualifications and experience, not those of its parent, sister, or subsidiary companies or its employees.
(i) Company registration/trade/license certificates issued by the relevant government authority in the country of establishment.
(ii) Company brochures indicating the firm's core business areas.
(iii) Completed Form (Annex: Form 1) providing information on similar contracts. This information should include the contract name and reference number, a brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, contract duration, the name of the client and the country in which the assignment was carried out, and the role of the Consultant in the contract. Copies of completion certificates or client references are not required at the EOI stage. However, at a later stage, during the proposal submission phase, the Client may request shortlisted consultants to submit such completion certificates.

data.project_name: Haiti Strengthening Public Financial Management Project
data.institution: Unité de Coordination de Projets du Ministère de l’Economie et des Finances
data.notice_text:
République d’Haïti

 

MINISTÈRE DE L’ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES (MEF)

 

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT

 

Approche de marché : Sélection de Consultant Individuel (INDV) par les emprunteurs de la banque mondiale

 

Titre du Projet : Haïti, Projet de Renforcement de la Gestion des Finances Publiques (PReGeFiP-P180384)

 

Mission : Elle consiste en l’élaboration de la stratégie sectorielle et du Cadre de Dépenses à Moyen Terme (CDMT) pour le secteur Santé

 

Numéro de Don : IDA E4170

 

Numéro de référence de l’AMI : 013

 

Numéro de référence du marché : HT-UCP/MEF-533946-CS-INDV

 

La République d’Haïti a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale (BM) en vue d’exécuter le Projet de Renforcement de la Gestion des Finances Publiques. Une partie du montant de ce don sera utilisée pour recruter un(e) consultant(e) qui sera chargé de l’élaboration de la stratégie sectorielle et du Cadre de Dépenses à Moyen Terme (CDMT) pour le secteur Santé

.

  1. Objectif :   

 

La mission du/de la consultant(e) national(e) consiste à élaborer, en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (MSPP), le MEF, le MPCE et les autres parties prenantes, une stratégie sectorielle et un CDMT, notamment : i) la définition des priorités stratégiques et les objectifs de performance du secteur ; ii) l’identification et la structuration des programmes budgétaires sectoriels ;-iii) l’établissement d’une programmation pluriannuelle des ressources financières cohérente et réaliste ; et iv) l’assurance de l’intégration de la stratégie sectorielle et du CDMT dans le SIGFiP et le cadre budgétaire national.

 

  1. Prestations attendues

 

Sous la supervision de la Direction Générale du Budget (DGB), le.a consultant,e aura pour principales tâches :

  • Document de stratégie sectorielle du secteur Santé validé ;
  • CDMT sectoriel triennal ou quinquennal validé et intégré dans le cadre budgétaire national ;
  • Référentiel d’indicateurs de performance sectoriels adopté ;
  • Plan de mise en œuvre et de suivi-évaluation disponible ;
  • Acteurs sectoriels formés sur l’utilisation de la stratégie et du CDMT.

 

  1. Durée

 

Les prestations s’étaleront sur une durée de Trente (30 jours ouvrables à l’intérieur d’une période de Trois (3) mois calendaires.

 

  1. Invitation

 

Le Ministère de l’Economie et des Finances (MEF) invite les consultants individuels compétents et qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services susmentionnés. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations, en français, démontrant qu’ils.elles possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services.  Les TDR pour cette mission sont annexés à la présente Sollicitation.

 

  1. Critère d’établissement de la liste restreinte 

 

Les consultants individuels intéressés seront sélectionnés sur la base de :

 

  • leurs expériences pertinentes pour cette mission.  Des références clients pourront en attester ;
  • leurs capacités techniques et managériales ;
  • leurs qualifications et leur disponibilité (CV détaillés inutiles) pour cette étape.

 

  1. Seuls les consultants retenus sur la liste restreinte recevront les Dossiers de Demande de Proposition (DDP)

  2. Les manifestations d’intérêt, en français, doivent être transmises par courrier électronique au plus tard le lundi 29 juin 2026 à 2 H 00 PM heure d’Haiti, aux adresses électroniques suivantes : ucp.secretariat@mef.gouv.ht et lys_faucher@yahoo.fr

TDR

ERMES DE REFERENCE

Recrutement d’un(e) consultant(e) pour l’élaboration de la stratégie sectorielle et du Cadre de Dépenses à Moyen Terme (CDMT) pour le secteur Santé

1. Contexte

Dans le cadre de la réforme de la gestion des finances publiques en Haïti et de la mise en œuvre progressive de la budgétisation par programme, le Gouvernement s’appuie sur le Système Intégré de Gestion des Finances Publiques (SIGFiP) comme outil central de planification, d’exécution et de suivi budgétaire.

Grâce à l’expérience acquise dans le cadre du PAGEFIS, plusieurs modules clés du SIGFiP ont déjà été configurés et testés avec succès :
- Administration et gestion de crédits, pour un suivi rigoureux des allocations et réallocations budgétaires ;
- Exécution budgétaire, assurant la traçabilité et le contrôle des engagements, liquidations et ordonnancements ;
- Immobilisations, facilitant la gestion du patrimoine public ;
- Comptabilité, garantissant la production d’états financiers fiables et conformes aux normes ;
- Planification budgétaire, fournissant des outils pour élaborer des prévisions et cadres budgétaires pluriannuels.

Ces acquis techniques et organisationnels offrent une base solide pour renforcer la planification sectorielle et intégrer les stratégies sectorielles dans le cadre budgétaire national.

Dans ce contexte, il est indispensable de doter le secteur Santé d’une stratégie sectorielle claire et d’un CDMT sectoriel aligné sur les priorités nationales, les Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) et les engagements internationaux du pays en matière de santé publique, de couverture sanitaire universelle et de résilience face aux crises sanitaires.

2. Objectif de la mission

Élaborer, en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population, le MEF, le MPCE et les autres parties prenantes, une stratégie sectorielle et un CDMT sectoriel pour le secteur Santé, afin de :
- Définir les priorités stratégiques et les objectifs de performance du secteur ;
- Identifier et structurer les programmes budgétaires sectoriels ;
- Établir une programmation pluriannuelle des ressources financières cohérente et réaliste ;
- Assurer l’intégration de la stratégie sectorielle et du CDMT dans le SIGFiP et le cadre budgétaire national.

3. Portée des travaux

Le/la consultant(e) mènera notamment les activités suivantes :

1. Analyse diagnostique du secteur
   - Évaluation des politiques, programmes et projets existants ;
   - Analyse des forces, faiblesses, opportunités et menaces (SWOT) du secteur ;
   - Identification des contraintes institutionnelles, techniques et financières.

2. Définition de la stratégie sectorielle
   - Formulation de la vision, de la mission et des objectifs stratégiques ;
   - Identification des axes prioritaires et des résultats attendus ;
   - Sélection des indicateurs de performance sectoriels (impact, résultat, produit).

3. Élaboration du CDMT sectoriel
   - Détermination des besoins financiers pluriannuels ;
   - Ventilation budgétaire par programme, action et activité ;
   - Alignement avec le Cadre Budgétaire à Moyen Terme (CBMT) national et les enveloppes indicatives.

4. Validation et intégration
   - Organisation d’ateliers de validation avec les parties prenantes ;
   - Intégration de la stratégie et du CDMT sectoriel dans le SIGFiP et les outils de suivi-évaluation.

4. Résultats attendus

- Document de stratégie sectorielle du secteur Santé validé ;
- CDMT sectoriel triennal ou quinquennal validé et intégré dans le cadre budgétaire national ;
- Référentiel d’indicateurs de performance sectoriels adopté ;
- Plan de mise en œuvre et de suivi-évaluation disponible ;
- Acteurs sectoriels formés sur l’utilisation de la stratégie et du CDMT.

5. Durée et calendrier

La mission est estimée à 30 jours ouvrables répartis sur une période de 3 mois, incluant les phases de diagnostic, d’élaboration, de validation et de finalisation des livrables.

6. Profil du/de la consultant(e)

- Diplôme supérieur (Bac+5) en santé publique, économie de la santé, planification, finances publiques, politiques publiques ou domaines connexes ;
- Expérience professionnelle confirmée (au moins 7 ans) en planification stratégique et budgétisation dans le secteur santé ;
- Maîtrise des approches de gestion axée sur les résultats et de la budgétisation par programme ;
- Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies sectorielles et/ou de CDMT sectoriels ;
- Bonne connaissance du contexte institutionnel et administratif haïtien ;
- Capacités avérées d’animation d’ateliers et de travail participatif.

7. Modalités de soumission

Les candidats intéressés devront soumettre :
- Un CV détaillé et actualisé ;
- Une note méthodologique présentant la compréhension de la mission, l’approche proposée et le calendrier indicatif ;
- Une offre financière ;
- Des références professionnelles pertinentes et exemples de travaux similaires.
