EQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

 

COUNTRY:   Federal Republic of Somalia (FRS)

PROJECT ID: P507443

Project Name: Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment

Post Title: Jubbaland State Liaison Officer

Reference No.: SO-MOLSA-566399-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Kismayo, Jubbaland, Somalia

 

Background

Jubbaland State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

SELECTION CRITERIA

Selection shall be based on the qualification and experience of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and skills should include:

Academic Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: development studies, social work, management, public administration or business administration or any other relevant fields;

Professional Experience

  1. Five (5) years of relevant working experience at the national or international level in project/program coordination and management areas including humanitarian organizations, international NGOs, and government.
  2. Demonstrated knowledge of the Somalia development agenda, mechanisms and principles of social protection, Safety net programs and intra-governmental processes;
  3. Proven skills and ability in effectively communicating with and coordinating across diverse groups of stakeholders, including project staff, partners, government authorities, private sector, communities as well as beneficiaries;
  4. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilization, or participatory development approaches.
  5. Excellent communication (spoken and written) skills in Somali and English, including the ability to communicate proactively with key stakeholders, correctly interpret messages from others and respond appropriately.

DURATION: The successful candidate will work under a one (1) year renewable contract based on competence and approval by MOLSA, Jubbaland state.

REPORTING OBLIGATIONS

The State Liaison Officer will directly report on a day-to-day basis to the Project Manager, Baxnaano through the Operations Team Lead. He/she will be expected to closely work with other Baxnaano PIU members for a smooth run of project operations. 

The Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, Federal Government of Somalai now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following: (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 references; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested applicants may refer further information including a detailed Terms of Reference in Annex I.    

Deadline: Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to this email procurement@baxnaano.gov.so and dg-mole@jubalandstate.so, copy the following emails as well Info@molsa.gov.so, dg-mole@jubalandstate.so Fardosa.Ahmed@baxnaano.gov.so and abdisalan.artan@baxnaano.gov.so,  on or before 16:00 hours 10th  October 2026, with email subject marked clearly as “Jubbaland State Liaison Officer, REF: SO-MOLSA-566399-CS-INDV

 

                        Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

 

 

 

 

 

                                            Annex I: Terms of Reference

                                   State Liaison Officer (Jubbaland)

           Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and

                               Youth Employment (P507443) Project

Background

Jubbaland State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

The program supports poor and vulnerable households through following components:

Component 1: Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today: Supports 28,000 youth (60% women & 5% disable persons) in urban areas with limited job opportunities and prolonged periods of inactivity, benefit from economic inclusion activities (wage and self-employment activities). contributing directly creating jobs and strengthening households’ resilience.

Component 2: Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow: The component will deliver regular cash transfers to 50,000 of the poorest households to meet basic needs, enhance climate-challenged food security, and prevent negative coping strategies during climate shocks, which in turn helps safeguard the human capital necessary for productive participation in the labor force. Approximately 10,000 shock affected poor and vulnerable households will be supported with emergency cash transfers as part of a contingent financing arrangement in case of climate shocks. 30,000 pregnant women and mothers with children under two will receive health- and nutrition-linked co-responsibility cash transfers (CCTs) to promote maternal and child health, reduce malnutrition, and improve early childhood development, strengthening the human capital necessary for future workforce productivity whilst mitigating adverse climate impacts. An early response-Health and Nutrition CCT will support 83,000 shock affected households with pregnant women and mothers with children under two to reduce the prevalence of significant acute malnutrition and infant mortality in drought affected prioritized districts. An education CCT program will target 5,000 children from the poorest and most climate-affected households, helping build the foundation required for long-term employability by increasing school enrollment and attendance.

Component 3: Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management: Supports enhancement of an adaptive social protection system, the National Socio-Economic Survey and project management including institutional capacity building for MoLSA. The objective of this support is to create a robust, efficient, and responsive social protection infrastructure. By strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing data management, strengthening the delivery system and registering the population in the USR, this component lays the foundation for sustainable and effective social protection and multisectoral poverty targeted investments. Under this component National Socio-economic Survey (NSES) will register 12 million people in Somalia in the USR collecting socio-economic data to inform targeting for pro-poor programs in the country. The component also provides support for effective project management, capacity building and oversight of project activities.

OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE OF WORK:

The State Liaison Officer will report to the Operations Team Lead and will be responsible for the implementation and delivery of all activities supported under the project. The State Liaison Officer must ensure compliance with operational protocols in the Baxnaano Operations Manual and accompanying guidelines, ensuring close coordination with relevant ministries, authorities, agencies and departments on day-to-day operational issues.

The Liaison Officer will help to coordinate the implementation of project activities at the State level between the PIU of the MoLSA, WFP and the relevant representatives of the Federal Member State (FMS), as well as other consultants (individuals and firms), hired under the project to facilitate effective delivery of project activities to achieve the overall project objectives. The Liaison Officer will work closely with the MOLSA PIU team and other implementing partners.

 

Under the leadership of the Operations Team Lead, duties of the State Liaison Officer will include:

 

  • Serve as a primary point of contact and sensitize the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level, community-based organizations (CBOs) and other social partners on social protection to create support for the project at the FMS level
  • Facilitate cooperation between the MoLSA/FGS and the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level on project activities and communicate priorities and concerns of the represented State to the PIU at the FGS level;
  • Coordinate with the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, as well as the CBOs and other social protection partners to support the implementation of the project in his/her state;
  • Attend and organize relevant meetings to support the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities, as requested by the representing State and the PIU/MoLSA
  • Prepare briefing notes, debriefs, reports necessary for the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities etc. and ensure follow-up on the represented State progress, as required;
  • Notify the PIU/MoLSA of pending and important issues to be raised during social protection meetings
  • Represent PIU at meetings, conferences and other relevant events at FMS level. Present PIUs position and safeguard its interest while coordinating with different stakeholders, in a professional manner. Share feedback and reports with PIU after attending the meetings/ events.
  • Recommend responses and action plans as a result of interacting with the project’s field team and the local community
  • Enable the flow of information between all relevant parties, particularly the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, including on potential risks and reporting immediately to the PIU/MoLSA complaints related to the Baxnaano in line with BOOST YOU complaints procedure for the PIU/MoLSA to respond as necessary;
  • Act as the State-level focal point for the project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), ensuring timely, transparent, and accountable handling of complaints Maintain proper documentation and reporting of grievances, ensuring confidentiality and data protection.
  • Support implementation and operationalization of the GRM in line with project procedures, including intake, registration, tracking, resolution, and feedback to complainants.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of SEA/SH cases and ensure information is shared only on a need-to-know basis in accordance with established protocols.
  • Facilitate immediate referral of SEA/SH survivors to appropriate service providers (health, psychosocial, legal) in line with the project’s referral pathway.
  • Immediately escalate high-risk complaints (including SEA/SH, fraud, or serious social conflict) to PIU following established protocols.
  • Assist PIU in organizing and coordinating USR survey related meetings, workshops and training sessions at FMS level.
  • Ensure affective planning in consultation with PIU and WFP teams to ensure execution of smooth USR survey activities in the FMS. Affectively coordinate with concerned FMS ministries and district administration to streamline the field activities of USR survey.
  • Coordinate deployment of survey teams in the field with concerned stakeholders including facilitation in provision of any approvals, field security and help in arrangement of logistics.
  • Collaborate with third party monitoring firms (hired by MoLSA)
  • Assist the Operations Team Lead in preparing periodic reports on the field activities and progress of surveys.
  • Assist in improving communication and information sharing between different stakeholders.
  • Liaise and coordinate with third party monitoring teams and ensure that all activities are carried out as per program design.
  • Oversee the activities of third party Beneficiary Communication and Outreach firm in liaison with PIU to ensure that the campaign is conducted as per the agreed SOPs.
  • Facilitate third party firms to complete their activities avoiding potential bottlenecks. Suggest improvements to PIU, based on lessons learned in the field.
  • In collaboration with relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, organize and participate in community sensitization and outreach activities to raise awareness to develop greater understanding of BOOST YOU and enhanced community partnership/commitment for the Baxnaano program;
  • Ensure that community engagement processes are culturally appropriate, accessible, gender-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive.
  • Facilitate regular community consultations, focus group discussions, and outreach sessions to enhance transparency and accountability of project interventions.
  • Monitor and report on stakeholder engagement activities, including participation levels, key concerns raised, and responses provided.
  • Compile and share reports about particular incidents, events, or updates on important issue for the project
  • Participate in trainings, workshops, supervision and implementation support missions conducted by the World Bank, and ‘learning-by-doing’ opportunities related to the BOOST YOU, as requested by the PIU;
  • Perform any other duties as required by PIU/ Operations Team Lead or Project Manager and/or represented FMS authority.

STATEMENT OF QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

The candidates should have the following desired qualifications:

  1. Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: development studies, social work, management, public administration or business administration or any other relevant fields;
  2. Five (5) years of relevant working experience at the national or international level in project/program coordination and management areas including humanitarian organizations, international NGOs, and government.
  3. Demonstrated knowledge of the Somalia development agenda, mechanisms and principles of social protection, Safety net programs and intra-governmental processes;
  4. Proven skills and ability in effectively communicating with and coordinating across diverse groups of stakeholders, including project staff, partners, government authorities, private sector, communities as well as beneficiaries;
  5. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilization, or participatory development approaches.
  6. Excellent communication (spoken and written) skills in Somali and English, including the ability to communicate proactively with key stakeholders, correctly interpret messages from others and respond appropriately. The candidate will demonstrate openness in sharing information;

CONDUCT OF WORK:

Reporting: The State Liaison Officer will directly report on a day-to-day basis to the Project Manager, Baxnaano through the Operations Team Lead. He/she will be expected to closely work with other Baxnaano PIU members for a smooth run of project operations. 

Language: Reports and other documents shall be submitted in English.

Duration of assignment: The successful candidate will work under a one (1) year renewable contract based on competence and approval by the Ministry.

Facilities to be provided: MoLSA will provide the office facilities, essential utilities, office services, stationery and office supplies and use of a computer and a printer.

Location of assignment: The duty station is in Kismayo, Jubbaland State of Somalia. The State Liaison Officer will be based at the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs or Baxnaano Offices.

Background

Southwest State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

The program supports poor and vulnerable households through following components:

Component 1: Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today: Supports 28,000 youth (60% women & 5% disable persons) in urban areas with limited job opportunities and prolonged periods of inactivity, benefit from economic inclusion activities (wage and self-employment activities). contributing directly creating jobs and strengthening households’ resilience.

Component 2: Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow: The component will deliver regular cash transfers to 50,000 of the poorest households to meet basic needs, enhance climate-challenged food security, and prevent negative coping strategies during climate shocks, which in turn helps safeguard the human capital necessary for productive participation in the labor force. Approximately 10,000 shock affected poor and vulnerable households will be supported with emergency cash transfers as part of a contingent financing arrangement in case of climate shocks. 30,000 pregnant women and mothers with children under two will receive health- and nutrition-linked co-responsibility cash transfers (CCTs) to promote maternal and child health, reduce malnutrition, and improve early childhood development, strengthening the human capital necessary for future workforce productivity whilst mitigating adverse climate impacts. An early response-Health and Nutrition CCT will support 83,000 shock affected households with pregnant women and mothers with children under two to reduce the prevalence of significant acute malnutrition and infant mortality in drought affected prioritized districts. An education CCT program will target 5,000 children from the poorest and most climate-affected households, helping build the foundation required for long-term employability by increasing school enrollment and attendance.

Component 3: Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management: Supports enhancement of an adaptive social protection system, the National Socio-Economic Survey and project management including institutional capacity building for MoLSA. The objective of this support is to create a robust, efficient, and responsive social protection infrastructure. By strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing data management, strengthening the delivery system and registering the population in the USR, this component lays the foundation for sustainable and effective social protection and multisectoral poverty targeted investments. Under this component National Socio-economic Survey (NSES) will register 12 million people in Somalia in the USR collecting socio-economic data to inform targeting for pro-poor programs in the country. The component also provides support for effective project management, capacity building and oversight of project activities.

OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE OF WORK:

The State Liaison Officer will report to the Operations Team Lead and will be responsible for the implementation and delivery of all activities supported under the project. The State Liaison Officer must ensure compliance with operational protocols in the Baxnaano Operations Manual and accompanying guidelines, ensuring close coordination with relevant ministries, authorities, agencies and departments on day-to-day operational issues.

The Liaison Officer will help to coordinate the implementation of project activities at the State level between the PIU of the MoLSA, WFP and the relevant representatives of the Federal Member State (FMS), as well as other consultants (individuals and firms), hired under the project to facilitate effective delivery of project activities to achieve the overall project objectives. The Liaison Officer will work closely with the MOLSA PIU team and other implementing partners.

Under the leadership of the Operations Team Lead, duties of the State Liaison Officer will include:

  • Serve as a primary point of contact and sensitize the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level, community-based organizations (CBOs) and other social partners on social protection to create support for the project at the FMS level
  • Facilitate cooperation between the MoLSA/FGS and the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level on project activities and communicate priorities and concerns of the represented State to the PIU at the FGS level;
  • Coordinate with the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, as well as the CBOs and other social protection partners to support the implementation of the project in his/her state;
  • Attend and organize relevant meetings to support the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities, as requested by the representing State and the PIU/MoLSA
  • Prepare briefing notes, debriefs, reports necessary for the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities etc. and ensure follow-up on the represented State progress, as required;
  • Notify the PIU/MoLSA of pending and important issues to be raised during social protection meetings
  • Represent PIU at meetings, conferences and other relevant events at FMS level. Present PIUs position and safeguard its interest while coordinating with different stakeholders, in a professional manner. Share feedback and reports with PIU after attending the meetings/ events.
  • Recommend responses and action plans as a result of interacting with the project’s field team and the local community
  • Enable the flow of information between all relevant parties, particularly the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, including on potential risks and reporting immediately to the PIU/MoLSA complaints related to the Baxnaano in line with BOOST YOU complaints procedure for the PIU/MoLSA to respond as necessary;
  • Act as the State-level focal point for the project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), ensuring timely, transparent, and accountable handling of complaints Maintain proper documentation and reporting of grievances, ensuring confidentiality and data protection.
  • Support implementation and operationalization of the GRM in line with project procedures, including intake, registration, tracking, resolution, and feedback to complainants.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of SEA/SH cases and ensure information is shared only on a need-to-know basis in accordance with established protocols.
  • Facilitate immediate referral of SEA/SH survivors to appropriate service providers (health, psychosocial, legal) in line with the project’s referral pathway.
  • Immediately escalate high-risk complaints (including SEA/SH, fraud, or serious social conflict) to PIU following established protocols.
  • Assist PIU in organizing and coordinating USR survey related meetings, workshops and training sessions at FMS level.
  • Ensure affective planning in consultation with PIU and WFP teams to ensure execution of smooth USR survey activities in the FMS. Affectively coordinate with concerned FMS ministries and district administration to streamline the field activities of USR survey.
  • Coordinate deployment of survey teams in the field with concerned stakeholders including facilitation in provision of any approvals, field security and help in arrangement of logistics.
  • Collaborate with third party monitoring firms (hired by MoLSA)
  • Assist the Operations Team Lead in preparing periodic reports on the field activities and progress of surveys.
  • Assist in improving communication and information sharing between different stakeholders.
  • Liaise and coordinate with third party monitoring teams and ensure that all activities are carried out as per program design.
  • Oversee the activities of third party Beneficiary Communication and Outreach firm in liaison with PIU to ensure that the campaign is conducted as per the agreed SOPs.
  • Facilitate third party firms to complete their activities avoiding potential bottlenecks. Suggest improvements to PIU, based on lessons learned in the field.
  • In collaboration with relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, organize and participate in community sensitization and outreach activities to raise awareness to develop greater understanding of BOOST YOU and enhanced community partnership/commitment for the Baxnaano program;
  • Ensure that community engagement processes are culturally appropriate, accessible, gender-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive.
  • Facilitate regular community consultations, focus group discussions, and outreach sessions to enhance transparency and accountability of project interventions.
  • Monitor and report on stakeholder engagement activities, including participation levels, key concerns raised, and responses provided.
  • Compile and share reports about particular incidents, events, or updates on important issue for the project
  • Participate in trainings, workshops, supervision and implementation support missions conducted by the World Bank, and ‘learning-by-doing’ opportunities related to the BOOST YOU, as requested by the PIU;
  • Perform any other duties as required by PIU/ Operations Team Lead or Project Manager and/or represented FMS authority.

STATEMENT OF QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

The candidates should have the following desired qualifications:

  1. Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: development studies, social work, management, public administration or business administration or any other relevant fields;
  2. Five (5) years of relevant working experience at the national or international level in project/program coordination and management areas including humanitarian organizations, international NGOs, and government.
  3. Demonstrated knowledge of the Somalia development agenda, mechanisms and principles of social protection, Safety net programs and intra-governmental processes;
  4. Proven skills and ability in effectively communicating with and coordinating across diverse groups of stakeholders, including project staff, partners, government authorities, private sector, communities as well as beneficiaries;
  5. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilization, or participatory development approaches.
  6. Excellent communication (spoken and written) skills in Somali and English, including the ability to communicate proactively with key stakeholders, correctly interpret messages from others and respond appropriately. The candidate will demonstrate openness in sharing information;

CONDUCT OF WORK:

Reporting: The State Liaison Officer will directly report on a day-to-day basis to the Project Manager, Baxnaano through the Operations Team Lead. He/she will be expected to closely work with other Baxnaano PIU members for a smooth run of project operations. 

Language: Reports and other documents shall be submitted in English.

Duration of assignment: The successful candidate will work under a one (1) year renewable contract based on competence and approval by the Ministry.

Facilities to be provided: MoLSA will provide the office facilities, essential utilities, office services, stationery and office supplies and use of a computer and a printer.

Location of assignment: The duty station is in Baidoa, Southwest State of Somalia. The State Liaison Officer will be based at the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs or Baxnaano Offices.

Terms of Reference

Project on the Construction, Publicity and Promotion of the High-Quality Food Standard System Implemented by Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation

Package IIQuality Monitoring, Inspection and Evaluation Services

In order to ensure the effective implementation of Package II (Quality Monitoring, Inspection and Evaluation Services) under the above-mentioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Demonstration Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to apply for a World Bank loan of USD10,000,000. Of this amount, Package II (Quality Monitoring, Inspection and Evaluation Services) under the abovementioned project plans to apply for a World Bank loan of USD 29.42 million (equivalent to RMB 2.03 million). It will provide targeted support for the achievement of project objectives through the following deliverables: engage a thirdparty institution to carry out quality monitoring, inspection and evaluation services; conduct quality monitoring of high-quality food in accordance with the inspection and testing requirements specified in high-quality food standards (including sensory requirements, quality indicators and partial safety indicators, with no fewer than 700 batches monitored within two years); and conduct on-site inspection and evaluation of high-quality food enterprises (no fewer than 20 enterprises covered within two years).

Expected outcomes of this project include tracking and evaluating the quality and safety status of high-quality food; ensuring that manufacturing and trading enterprises of high-quality food as well as the high-quality food products themselves consistently comply with the requirements of high-quality food standards; establishing and maintaining the credibility of high-quality food brands; and enhancing consumer trust in high-quality food.

2.Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of advancing quality monitoring, inspection and evaluation services, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel under market regulation. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as“proportion of early-warnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". The core objectives are to build a premium brand image of high-quality food, to formulate evaluation and management specifications for high-quality food, to utilize multiple approaches including on-site inspection and evaluation and quality monitoring to track and evaluate the quality and safety status of high-quality food, thereby comprehensively safeguarding quality and safety of high-quality food, and promoting the improvement of food quality and the high-quality development of the food industry.

3. Scope of Services

Total investment for this project amounts to RMB 2.03 million.

3.1 Scope of Service Recipients

Service recipients cover the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation, as well as provincial, municipal and district/countylevel market regulation authorities. Target users include the general public and highquality food manufacturing and trading enterprises, among others.

3.2 Service Content

This project requires the contractor to provide services with capabilities for independent technical assessment and compliance verification. Specific work contents are as follows:  First, conduct quality monitoring of high-quality food in accordance with the requirements of Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation and based on the test items and test methods specified in high-quality food standards. Testing items shall include sensory requirements, quality indicators, and partial safety indicators. The contractor shall perform statistical analysis on the test results, assess whether the results comply with the requirements of the high-quality food standards, and issue a test report. The testing institution shall formulate an annual sampling plan, ensuring that the sampled products cover as many categories of high-quality food as possible. No fewer than 700 batches shall be monitored within two years. Second, the contractor shall organize on-site inspections of high-quality food manufacturing and trading entities, and conduct evaluations on the whole process, including supplier management, base management, quality management at key control points for production and operation, warehousing and logistics management, personnel management, and system development of enterprises, so as to ensure that high-quality food products consistently meet the standard requirements. The inspection institution shall formulate an annual inspection and evaluation plan, aiming to cover as many implementing entities as possible. No fewer than 20 enterprises shall be covered within two years . Where quality monitoring or on-site inspection confirms that an enterprise or product fails to comply with high-quality food standards but meets food safety standards, the relevant information shall be promptly reported to the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation. The relevant products shall be removed from the special sales zones for high-quality food, and the “Greater Bay Area Standard”logo on product outer packaging shall be revoked. The application for reinstatement of the “GBA Standard” logo can be submitted only after the completion of rectification and when test results prove the product complies with high-quality food standards.Where quality monitoring or on-site inspection confirms that an enterprise or product fails to meet food safety standards, the relevant information shall be promptly reported to the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation. Meanwhile, the contractor shall urge the enterprise to recall and shelf-remove the products and complete corresponding rectification. See Appendix 1 for further details.

3.3 Service Period

The service period shall commence on the date of contract signing and end on the project closure date (March 31, 2029).

Requirements

1

Quality monitoring, inspection and evaluation

Conduct high-quality food quality monitoring in accordance with the requirements of the project, no fewer than 700 batches monitored within two years.

(1) Frequency of sampling and testing

The volume of sampling and testing for high-quality foods should increase annually in line with the volume of such foods circulating in the market; Priority shall be given to the sampling and inspection of highquality food products that fall under any of the following categories: those newly included in the high-quality food list in the current year; those with large consumption volume across Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao; those with non-compliance or failure records in supervision samplinginspection or high-quality food quality monitoring over the past two years; and those whose manufacturers have been classified as Level-C or Level-D by the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation in accordance with the Measures for Risk-based Classification Management of Food and Food-Related Product Manufacturers of Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation (Trial)

(2) Selection of sampling site

Sampling and inspection for high-quality food products should comprehensively cover all types of online and offline business entities, ensuring that regulatory oversight is thorough and quality assurance is guaranteed. For online channels, sampling efforts should focus on mainstream e-commerce platforms (such as Tmall, JD.com, and Pinduoduo), fresh food delivery platforms, as well as the rapidly growing live-streaming commerce model in recent years (including brand self-hosted livestreams, influencer livestream rooms, and product links on short-video platforms). For offline channels, sampling shall cover physical sales terminals such as supermarkets, convenience stores and agricultural trade markets. By coordinating the sampling layout across both online and offline channels, a comprehensive and multi-dimensional supervision system can be established, so as to effectively ensure that consumers can obtain authentic, safe and highquality product experience when purchasing high-quality food through any channels.

(3) Test items

Test items shall strictly comply with the relevant provisions on inspection and testing specified in high-quality food standards,ensuring comprehensive coverage of the three core aspects explicitly required: first, sensory requirements—including the color, odor, taste, and texture of high-quality foods, which are visually distinguishable characteristics designed to ensure that the product meets consumers' sensory expectations for high quality; second, quality indicators—such as moisture content, fat content, protein content, peroxide value, and soluble solids—which are key parameters reflecting the intrinsic quality of the product and guarantee its authenticity and superior quality; third, the selection of safety indicators shall be based on risk assessment results, covering limit values for substances that may affect human health, such as heavy metals (e.g., lead, cadmium, arsenic), mycotoxins (e.g., aflatoxins), pesticide residues, and the levels of food additive usage. These approaches ensures that high-quality foods not only meet stringent quality requirements but also provide adequate safety assurance.

2

Inspection and Evaluation of high-quality food enterprises in accordance with the requirements of the project (no fewer than 20 enterprises covered within two years)

  1. Priority inspection targets

Priority shall be given to the inspection and evaluation of enterprises falling under any of the following categories: enterprises whose food products manufactured have no records of non-compliance or failure in supervision samplinginspection or high-quality food quality monitoring over the past two years; enterprises classified as Level-C or Level-D by the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation in accordance with the Measures for Risk-based Classification Management of Food and Food-Related Product Manufacturers of Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation (Trial); enterprises whose products are newly included in the high-quality food list in the current year; and enterprises that have not been connected to the high-quality food traceability platform

(2) Key inspection content

Enterprise inspections shall cover key links across the whole chain of high-quality food production, storage, transportation, and sales chain, including raw material control (e.g., supplier qualification review and raw material base management), key control points during the production process (e.g., real-time record of process parameters such as processing temperature and duration),  authenticity of traceability data (cross-check against data from high-quality food traceability platforms), and the usage of the "GBA Standard" logo; so as to ensure full process control from source to customers.
